summary: The paper proves the Ramanujan conjecture (Theorem A) and the Sato–Tate conjecture (Theorem B) for regular algebraic cuspidal representations of GL_2 of parallel weight over imaginary CM fields, hence for all Bianchi modular forms of weight ≥ 2 (Theorems E–G). Both follow from purity and potential automorphy of all symmetric powers of rank-2 compatible systems with Hodge–Tate weights {0, m} (Theorems C, 6.2.1, 7.2.1). Three new ingredients: (1) Theorem D: for p > n the special fibre of every weight-0 crystalline lifting ring is generically reduced, proved on the Emerton–Gee stack by computing extensions of rank-one Breuil modules (§2); (2) an automorphy lifting theorem in weight 0 with p arbitrarily ramified (Theorem 3.2.1), from Caraiani–Newton's local–global compatibility and derived Ihara avoidance, where Theorem D supplies the unique generalisation of generic points; (3) a p–r switch between Sym^{n−1}R ⊗ R_aux and Sym^{n−1}R ⊗ R_CM, where R_aux and S_UA come from Qian's non-self-dual Dwork motives in the new unitary case p ≡ −1 mod N, made crystalline ordinary by Drinfeld–Kedlaya (§§4, 6). The endpoints are planned in ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.2, ML.3). §2 goes to a new Part II of LocalGaloisDeformationRings, §3 to a new Part II of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, and §4 with the switching construction to the pending Dwork Part II of PAPER-QIAN-23. The remaining lemmas are sources of existing layers (ML, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations, ArithmeticGaloisDuality, PA.5, R23.1, L7). Thirteen source issues are recorded, one already corrected by the authors. After review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): 146 items (5 library, 36 planned, 105 missing), 9 routes, all accepted. E1–E13 are confirmed (E7 restated without a sign convention) and E14–E32 are new. The substantive new findings concern the potential automorphy argument of §§5–6: hypothesis (13) of Proposition 6.2.3 is inconsistent with (8b) for m > 2 and the proof of Theorem 6.2.4 asserts a false image (E29); Proposition 6.2.3 lacks the crystallinity of r_𝔯 at r (E30); Lemma 5.2.6 needs absolute irreducibility (E28) and a square α (E27); the m = 2 case of Lemma 5.2.4 (E31) and the second F^avoid (E32) need strengthening; Proposition 4.4.2 needs η compatible with the pairings (E23). All have direct repairs, and none affects Theorems A–D or 6.2.1.

items.name: Theorem A (Theorem 7.1.1): the Ramanujan conjecture in parallel weight over imaginary CM fields
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) of parallel weight (Definition 1.5.1). Then for every finite place v of F, π_v is (essentially) tempered. In the normalisation of Theorem A (π cuspidal algebraic of parallel weight k ≥ 2, i.e. of weight (k − 2, 0)_τ after twist): π_v is tempered for all finite v, and for v prime to the level the eigenvalues α_v, β_v of rec^T_{F_v}(π_v)(Frob_v) satisfy |α_v| = |β_v| = N(v)^{(k−1)/2} (Lemma 7.2.2 gives q_v^{w/2} for rec_{F_v}, and the rec^T shift contributes q_v^{1/2}).
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3 integrates symmetric-power automorphy and its analytic consequences; purity of the compatible system is deduced from potential automorphy of all symmetric powers (Lemma 6.1.3, Theorem 6.2.1). Proof: twist to weight (m − 1, 0) using Clozel's purity lemma, make ψ∘N_{F′/F} a square after a quadratic CM extension (as in ACC+ Theorem 7.1.1), reduce to unramified π_v by solvable base change (ACC+ Corollary 7.1.15), then use the trichotomy of ACC+ Lemma 7.1.2 (induced: purity of rank one; Artin up to twist: excluded by distinct Hodge–Tate weights; strongly irreducible: Theorem 6.2.1). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the normalisation of the Satake parameters was made explicit; Theorem A says 'tempered', Theorem 7.1.1 '(essentially) tempered'.

items.name: Theorem B (Theorem 7.2.3): the Sato–Tate conjecture in parallel weight over imaginary CM fields
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field and π a non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) of weight λ and parallel weight, with λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,2} = w and central character |·|^{−w}ψ, ψ unitary of type A_0. Let S_π be the set of finite places at which π is ramified (printed: 'unramified'; see sourceIssues E13). Then the classes [π_v] ∈ ST(π), v ∉ S_π, are equidistributed with respect to the Haar probability measure μ_ST of ST(π): for every continuous conjugation-invariant f : ST(π) → ℂ, lim_{X→∞} Σ_{v∉S_π, q_v<X} f([π_v]) / #{v ∉ S_π : q_v < X} = ∫_{ST(π)} f dμ_ST. Theorem B is the case where the normalised a_v are real: they are equidistributed for (2/π)√(1 − x²)dx.
items.note: ML.3 plans Sato–Tate via symmetric powers, with the analytic inputs for the Weyl criterion supplied separately (AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4). Proof: Serre's criterion; the L-functions L^{S_π}(π, ρ, s) are handled from potential automorphy of Sym^{n−1}R as in Gee 2009 §7 and BLGHT11 §8, R being strongly irreducible by ACC+ Lemma 7.1.2 and non-CM.

items.name: Theorem C (Theorem 7.2.1): purity and potential automorphy of symmetric powers of rank-2 compatible systems
items.statement: Let F be a CM field and R = (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_λ}, {H_τ}) a very weakly compatible system of rank 2 representations of G_F with H_τ = {0, m} for all τ, for some m ≥ 1. (1) If R is strongly irreducible, then R is pure of weight m, and for each n ≥ 1 there is a finite CM extension F′/F, Galois over ℚ, such that Sym^{n−1}R|_{G_{F′}} is automorphic. (2) If R is irreducible but not strongly irreducible, then R is pure of weight m and for each n ≥ 1, Sym^{n−1}R is a direct sum of automorphic compatible systems of dimension at most 2. (The introduction's Theorem C states this for systems whose Frobenius polynomials are independent of λ — printed 'of v', sourceIssues E1 — and adds potential automorphy of R itself.)
items.locator: §1, Theorem C, p. 4; §7.2, Theorem 7.2.1 and proof, pp. 61–62
items.note: ML.2 assembles potential automorphy and ML.3 owns the symmetric-power endpoints. Proof: reduce to det r_λ = ε^{−m} as in Theorem 7.1.1 and apply Theorem 6.2.1; the non-strongly-irreducible case is induced from algebraic Hecke characters of a quadratic extension (ACC+ Lemma 7.1.2).

items.name: Theorem 6.2.1: purity and potential automorphy for det r_λ = ε^{−m}
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field and R a very weakly compatible system of rank 2 representations of G_F. Let m ≥ 1 and suppose (1) H_τ = {0, m} for each τ; (2) det r_λ = ε^{−m}; (3) R is strongly irreducible. Then R is pure of weight m, and for each n ≥ 1 there is a finite CM extension F_n/F, Galois over ℚ, such that Sym^{n−1}R|_{G_{F_n}} is automorphic.
items.note: ML.2/ML.3. For m = 1 this is ACC+ Corollary 7.1.12. For m ≥ 2: Theorem 6.2.4 gives weak automorphy of level prime to {v | v_0}; Lemma 6.1.3 gives purity at v_0, arbitrary; Lemma 6.1.4 upgrades weak automorphy to automorphy.

items.name: Definition 1.5.1: parallel weight, and Clozel's purity lemma for GL_2 over CM fields
items.statement: π is regular algebraic of weight λ = (λ_{τ,1} ≥ λ_{τ,2})_τ if the infinitesimal character of π_∞ is that of V_λ^∨. A regular algebraic π of GL_2(𝔸_F) of weight λ is of parallel weight if λ_{τ,1} − λ_{τ,2} is independent of τ, equivalently if π has a regular algebraic twist of weight μ = (m − 1, 0)_τ for some m ≥ 1; it has parallel weight k ≥ 2 if μ = (k − 2, 0)_τ. For F imaginary CM and π cuspidal regular algebraic of weight λ there is w ∈ ℤ with λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,2} = w for all τ (Clozel's purity lemma [Clo90, Lemma 4.9]); hence λ_{τ,1} − λ_{τ,2} = λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τc,2}, and every such π over an imaginary quadratic field has parallel weight.
items.locator: §1.5, Definition 1.5.1 and the following paragraph, p. 11
items.note: Routed to ML.0 (the registry of automorphic objects, infinity types and normalisations). Regular algebraic weights are planned in AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.0; the parallel-weight condition and Clozel's purity lemma are not. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the definition of regular algebraic of weight λ, which precedes Definition 1.5.1, was added; the 'equivalently' (a twist to weight (m − 1, 0)_τ) is justified in the paper only for cuspidal π over CM fields, via Clozel's lemma, which is the only use. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected to the published page numbers.

items.name: Bianchi modular forms, their Fourier coefficients and parabolic cohomology with Hecke operators
items.statement: For F imaginary quadratic, a cuspidal Bianchi modular eigenform f of level 𝔫 and weight k (a collection of h_F functions on hyperbolic 3-space, or adelically a vector in a regular algebraic cuspidal π) has Fourier coefficients c(𝔭, f), normalised so that c(O_F, f) = 1 [Wil17 §1.2, Hid94 §6]. For k, l ≥ 2, H = H¹(Γ_1(𝔫), Sym^{k−2}ℂ² ⊗ \overline{Sym^{l−2}ℂ²}) (the second factor complex-conjugated) with parabolic subspace H_par (classes vanishing on every parabolic subgroup, i.e. on the Borel–Serre boundary of Y_1(𝔫) = ℍ³/Γ_1(𝔫)); Hecke operators T_𝔭 for principal 𝔭 = (π) ∤ 𝔫 via A = diag(π, 1); for h_F > 1 replace Y_1(𝔫) by the union of Y_1(𝔫; 𝔞), 𝔞 running over representatives of Cl(O_F) prime to 𝔫. H_par = 0 unless k = l [Har87, 3.6.1], and the Eichler–Shimura isomorphism [Har87 §3.6] sends f to a Hecke eigenclass η_f ∈ H_par with T_𝔭-eigenvalue c(𝔭, f).
items.note: Routed to ML.0 with Theorems E–G. The cohomology of arithmetic groups with Hecke correspondences and Borel–Serre boundary is planned in ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (ALS.1, ALS.3, ALS.4); the Bianchi Fourier expansion and Harder's Eichler–Shimura comparison are not. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): material correction: the coefficient system is Sym^{k−2}ℂ² ⊗ \overline{Sym^{l−2}ℂ²}, with the complex conjugate (pp. 8–9, visible on the page images); without it the local system and the vanishing statement change. The class-group representatives are prime to 𝔫, and c(O_F, f) = 1.

items.name: Theorem E: the Ramanujan bound for Fourier coefficients of Bianchi eigenforms
items.statement: Let F be imaginary quadratic and f a cuspidal Bianchi modular eigenform of level 𝔫 and weight k, normalised so that c(O_F, f) = 1, and 𝔭 a prime of O_F not dividing 𝔫. Then |c(𝔭, f)| ≤ 2N(𝔭)^{(k−1)/2}.
items.note: Corollary of Theorem A; routed to ML.3 with the Bianchi applications. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the normalisation c(O_F, f) = 1 (p. 8) was added.

items.name: Theorem F: the Ramanujan bound for Hecke eigenvalues on parabolic cohomology of Bianchi manifolds
items.statement: Let 𝔭 be a principal prime of O_F not dividing 𝔫 and a_𝔭 an eigenvalue of T_𝔭 on H_par. Then |a_𝔭| ≤ 2N(𝔭)^{(k−1)/2}.
items.note: From Theorem E by the Eichler–Shimura isomorphism [Har87]; routed to ML.3.

items.name: Theorem G: mass equidistribution for level-one Bianchi eigenforms
items.statement: Assume F has class number one. For any sequence of Bianchi modular eigenforms f of level one and weight tending to ∞, the measures μ_f [Mar11 §3] converge weakly to the hyperbolic volume on Y = SL_2(O_F)\ℍ³.
items.note: Marshall's [Mar11, Cor. 3] assumed the Ramanujan conjecture ([Mar12]); Theorem E supplies it. Routed to ML.3 as an analytic application; Marshall's theorem is a prerequisite.

items.name: Hodge–Tate conventions, weight 0 and the lifting rings R^□ and R^{crys,0,O}
items.statement: For K/ℚ_p finite and σ : K ↪ ℚ̄_p, HT_σ(ρ) is the multiset with i of multiplicity dim (W ⊗_{σ,K} K̂(i))^{G_K}; ε has HT_σ(ε) = {−1}. A d-dimensional ρ has weight 0 if HT_σ(ρ) = {0, 1, …, d − 1} for all σ. For ρ̄ : G_K → GL_d(𝔽) and E/ℚ_p containing the Galois closure of K, R^{□,O}_{ρ̄} is the universal lifting ring and R^{crys,0,O}_{ρ̄} its quotient characterised by: an O-algebra map R^□ → B to a finite flat E-algebra B factors through it iff the corresponding representation is crystalline of weight 0 (the paper gives no reference; this is Kisin's ring [Kis08]); R^{□,O′} = R^{□,O} ⊗_O O′ for finite extensions of coefficients [BLGGT14, Lemma 1.2.1].
items.note: Hodge–Tate weights: PadicHodgeTheory R06.2. Kisin's potentially semistable lifting rings of fixed labelled Hodge type in rank n, with characteristic-zero points, flatness and dimension: LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (rank 2: R08.3); unrestricted lifting rings: R08.1. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the characterisation is through finite flat E-algebras, not only through ℚ̄_p-points; [BLGGT14, Lemma 1.2.1] is cited only for the unrestricted ring.

items.name: Local Langlands normalisations rec_K and rec^T_K
items.statement: Art_K sends uniformisers to geometric Frobenius elements; rec_K is the local Langlands correspondence of Harris–Taylor; rec^T_K is its Tate-normalised form [CT14 §2.1] (rec^T_K(π) = rec_K(π ⊗ |det|^{(1−n)/2})), used for Hecke polynomials and in Definition 6.1.2, while Lemma 7.2.2 uses rec_{F_v}.
items.note: The arbitrary-rank local Langlands construction and its normalisations are EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6; ML.0 keeps the normalisation register. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the Art_K normalisation (p. 10) was added; the paper cites [CT14, §2.1] for rec^T and does not print its formula; Lemma 7.2.2 uses rec, not rec^T.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin modules with 𝔽-coefficients and étale φ-modules
items.statement: For K/ℚ_p with residue field k, ramification index e, uniformiser π and Eisenstein polynomial E(u) with E(0) = p, and K_∞ = K(π^{1/p^∞}): a Breuil–Kisin module of height ≤ h with 𝔽-coefficients is a finite free 𝔖_𝔽 = (k ⊗ 𝔽)[[u]]-module 𝔐 with φ-semilinear φ such that the cokernel of the linearisation is killed by E(u)^h = u^{eh}; T_∞(M) = (M ⊗ k((u))^sep)^{φ=1} is an equivalence from étale φ-modules to G_{K_∞}-representations [Fon90, Kis09 1.1.12].
items.note: Breuil–Kisin modules and the height bound from the Eisenstein polynomial: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4; the étale φ-module equivalence over K_∞ is part of the same comparison (with PadicHodgeTheory P7 owning étale (φ,Γ)-modules). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the paper says 'finite free'.

items.name: Quasi-Breuil modules, Breuil modules with monodromy and crystalline Breuil modules
items.statement: Let S_𝔽 = 𝔖_𝔽/u^{ep} and 0 ≤ h ≤ p − 2. A quasi-Breuil module of height h is a finite free S_𝔽-module M with a submodule M_h ⊇ u^{eh}M and a φ-semilinear φ_h : M_h → M whose image generates M; 𝔐 ↦ S_𝔽 ⊗_{φ,𝔖_𝔽} 𝔐 is an equivalence from Breuil–Kisin modules of height ≤ h [Bre99, Thm. 4.1.1]. Let c be the image of φ(E(u))/p in S_𝔽 (a unit, c = φ(d)). A Breuil module is a quasi-Breuil module with N : M → M satisfying N(sx) = sN(x) + N(s)x (N = −u d/du on S_𝔽), u^eN(M_h) ⊆ M_h and φ(u^eN(x)) = cN(φ(x)) for x ∈ M_h; it is crystalline if N(M) ⊆ uM. The published text takes c = 1 (Remark 2.1.1); its footnote 2 and arXiv v3 correct this (sourceIssues E2).
items.note: Routed to the new Part II WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. R07.4 plans Breuil–Kisin modules but not Breuil's S-modules with monodromy.

items.name: Theorem 2.1.4: exactness and the subobject correspondence for crystalline Breuil modules
items.statement: (1) The categories FBrMod^cr and FqBrMod are exact categories [Qui10], and the functors T (T(M) = Hom(M, Â)^∨ [HLM17 (A.3.1)]) and T_∞ are exact. (2) For M in FBrMod^cr, N ↦ image of T(N) ↪ T(M) is an order-preserving bijection Θ from Breuil submodules of M to G_K-subrepresentations of T(M), with Θ(M_2)/Θ(M_1) ≅ T(M_2/M_1).
items.note: Proof from [Car11, Thm. 2.1.2] and [HLM17, Props. 2.3.4, 2.3.5], with the duality of [EGH13, Def. 3.2.8]. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings.

items.name: Theorem 2.1.5: reductions of crystalline lattices come from crystalline Breuil modules
items.statement: Let ρ : G_K → GL_n(O) be a lattice in a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, h], 0 ≤ h ≤ p − 2, and ρ̄ its reduction. Then there is a crystalline Breuil module M with 𝔽-coefficients with ρ̄ ≅ T(M); its underlying Breuil–Kisin module has height ≤ h and is the reduction of the Breuil–Kisin module with O-coefficients of ρ|_{G_{K_∞}}.
items.note: Proof via strongly divisible modules [Liu08 Thm. 2.3.5, Cor. 3.3.2], [EGH13 Prop. 3.1.4, Lem. 3.2.2], [GLS14]: N vanishes modulo u on the crystalline strongly divisible module. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected to the published page numbers.

items.name: Rank-one Breuil–Kisin modules 𝔐(s; a) and the invariants α_i
items.statement: For s = (s_i) ∈ ℤ_{≥0}^f and a ∈ 𝔽^×, 𝔐(s; a) is the rank-one Breuil–Kisin module with basis e_i of 𝔐_i and φ(e_{i−1}) = (a)_i u^{s_i} e_i [GLS14, Lem. 6.2]; α_i(𝔐(s; a)) = (1/(p^f − 1)) Σ_j p^{f−j} s_{j+i}; with (a)_0 = a and (a)_i = 1 for i ≠ 0, every rank-one Breuil–Kisin module with F̄_p-coefficients is isomorphic to exactly one 𝔐(s; a); a nonzero map 𝔐(s; a) → 𝔐(t; b) exists iff α_i(𝔐(s; a)) − α_i(𝔐(t; b)) ∈ ℤ_{≥0} for all i and a = b ([GLS15, Lem. 5.1.2]).
items.note: Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected to p. 16; the criterion for nonzero maps was stated (the review checked it: m_i = p·m_{i−1} + t_i − s_i is solved by m_i = α_i(s) − α_i(t)).

items.name: Lemma 2.2.3: rank-one crystalline Breuil modules
items.statement: If each s_i ∈ [0, e(p − 2)], the rank-one Breuil–Kisin module 𝔐(s; a) underlies a unique height-(p − 2) Breuil module M(s; a), with M^{p−2}_j = ⟨u^{e(p−2)−s_j}(1 ⊗ e_{j−1})⟩, φ(u^{e(p−2)−s_j}(1 ⊗ e_{j−1})) = (a)_j(1 ⊗ e_j) and N(1 ⊗ e_{j−1}) = 0; in particular it is crystalline.
items.note: The proof uses the φ–N commutation (with the unit c of sourceIssues E2, as in arXiv v3). Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected to the published page numbers.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.4: normal form of extensions of rank-one Breuil–Kisin modules
items.statement: Every extension 𝔐 of 𝔐(s; a) by 𝔐(t; b) has bases e_i, f_i of 𝔐_i with φ(e_{i−1}) = (b)_i u^{t_i} e_i and φ(f_{i−1}) = (a)_i u^{s_i} f_i + y_i e_i, where y_i ∈ 𝔽[u] has degree < s_i, except that when there is a nonzero map 𝔐(s; a) → 𝔐(t; b) one y_j may also have a term of degree s_j + α_j(𝔐(s; a)) − α_j(𝔐(t; b)).
items.note: This is [GLS15, Prop. 5.1.3]. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected to the published page numbers.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.7: crystallinity constrains the extension polynomials
items.statement: Let M be a crystalline Breuil module which is an extension of M(s; a) by M(t; b), with underlying Breuil–Kisin module as in Proposition 2.2.4. Then each y_j has no nonzero terms of degree l with l < s_j − e + max(n_{j+1}, 1) and l ≢ t_j (mod p), where n_i := (p^f − 1)^{−1} Σ_{j=1}^f p^{f−j}(s_{j+i−1} − t_{j+i−1} − e) (2.2.8).
items.note: The proof solves the φ–N commutation relation degree by degree (the constants c and d of sourceIssues E2 enter (2.2.9)). Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected; (2.2.8) stated explicitly.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.13 and the invariants n_i, r_i
items.statement: With n_i as in (2.2.8), which satisfy n_j + (s_{j−1} − t_{j−1} − e) = p·n_{j−1} (2.2.12), and r_i := s_i − t_i − e + ⌊n_{i+1}⌋ − p⌊n_i⌋ + 1 (2.2.14) (so that s_i + ⌊n_{i+1}⌋ − e + 1 ≡ t_i + r_i mod p), one has r_i ∈ [1, p] for every i.
items.note: Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected; (2.2.12) and (2.2.14) stated explicitly.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.15: restriction to K_∞ and its image
items.statement: For characters χ_1 = T(M(t; b)), χ_2 = T(M(s; a)): (1) res_{K_∞} : Ext¹_{G_K}(χ_2, χ_1) → Ext¹_{G_{K_∞}}(χ_2, χ_1) is injective unless χ_1χ_2^{−1} = ε̄, when its kernel is the très ramifiée line of the Kummer extension of the chosen π; (2) its image has dimension [K : ℚ_p], or [K : ℚ_p] + 1 if χ_1 = χ_2; (3) the étale φ-modules in the image are exactly those with a basis in which φ(e_{i−1}) = (b)_i u^{t_i} e_i and φ(f_{i−1}) = (a)_i u^{s_i} f_i + y_i e_i with y_i ∈ 𝔽[u, u^{−1}] supported in degrees [s_i + ⌊n_{i+1}⌋ − e + 1, s_i + ⌊n_{i+1}⌋] (with one extra term of degree s_i + (p^f − 1)^{−1}Σ_j p^{f−j}(s_{j+i} − t_{j+i}) allowed for one i when χ_1 = χ_2).
items.note: Proof from [GLS15 Lem. 5.4.2, Thm. 5.1.5, Prop. 5.3.4, Thm. 5.4.1, Thm. 6.1.18], [CEGM17 Thm. 3.3.2], [Ste22 Thm. 4.2], [CEGS22b Lem. A.4]. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected; the extra degree stated. The proof has two misprints (sourceIssues E16, E17).

items.name: Lemma 2.2.18: a combinatorial consequence of Σ(s_j − t_j − e) < 0
items.statement: If Σ_{j=1}^f (s_j − t_j − e) < 0 then there is i with either ⌊n_{i+1}⌋ = −1 and r_i ≠ p, or ⌊n_{i+1}⌋ ≤ −2.
items.note: Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected to the published page numbers.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.19: crystalline rank-one Breuil extensions do not exhaust Ext¹
items.statement: If Σ_{j=1}^f (s_j − t_j − e) < 0, then the restriction map Ext¹_{BrMod^cr}(M(s; a), M(t; b)) → Ext¹_{G_K}(χ_2, χ_1) is not surjective.
items.note: The key local computation: an explicit étale φ-module in the image of res_{K_∞} (Lemma 2.2.15(3)) has a term forbidden by Lemma 2.2.7. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected to the published page numbers.

items.name: Definition 2.2.26: generic extension classes
items.statement: For characters χ_1, χ_2 : G_K → 𝔽̄_p^×, a class in Ext¹_{G_K}(χ_2, χ_1) is generic if it is not in the image of Ext¹_{BrMod^cr}(M(s; a), M(t; b)) → Ext¹_{G_K}(χ_2, χ_1) for any rank-one Breuil modules with T(M(t; b)) = χ_1, T(M(s; a)) = χ_2 and Σ_j (s_j − t_j − e) < 0. By Lemma 2.2.19 the generic classes form the complement of finitely many proper subspaces (Remark 2.2.27).
items.note: Remark 2.2.29 concerns Breuil–Kisin modules of irreducible crystalline G_{ℚ_p}-representations with Hodge–Tate weights 0, p + 2 and explains why the method stops at weights [0, p − 2]; it does not show that p > d is necessary (Remark 2.5.7 calls the case p ≤ d plausible). Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected; the gloss on Remark 2.2.29 was corrected.

items.name: Definition 2.3.1: generic residual representations
items.statement: ρ̄ : G_K → GL_d(𝔽) is generic if it is upper triangular with diagonal characters χ_d, χ_{d−1}, …, χ_1 (top to bottom) and each off-diagonal extension class in Ext¹_{G_K}(χ_i, χ_{i+1}), i = 1, …, d − 1, is generic in the sense of Definition 2.2.26.
items.note: Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings.

items.name: Theorem 2.3.2: weight-0 crystalline lifts of generic ρ̄ are ordinary
items.statement: Suppose p > d and ρ : G_K → GL_d(O) is weight 0 crystalline with ρ̄ generic. Then ρ is upper triangular with diagonal ur_{λ_d}, ur_{λ_{d−1}}ε^{−1}, …, ur_{λ_1}ε^{1−d} for some λ_1, …, λ_d ∈ O^×.
items.note: Induction on d using Theorem 2.1.5, Theorem 2.1.4(2) and Lemma 2.2.19, with [Kis09 Prop. 1.2.11], [Liu07 §3.1], [Kis06 Prop. 1.3.15], [Kis10 Thm. 1.2.1]. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected to the published page numbers.

items.name: Corollary 2.3.3: generic ρ̄ with a weight-0 crystalline lift
items.statement: If ρ̄ : G_K → GL_d(𝔽) is generic and has a weight-0 crystalline lift, then ρ̄ is upper triangular with diagonal ur_{λ̄_d}, ur_{λ̄_{d−1}}ε̄^{−1}, …, ur_{λ̄_1}ε̄^{1−d}, and the off-diagonal extensions are peu ramifiées.
items.note: Peu ramifiée from [CEGS22b, Lem. A.4]. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings.

items.name: Proposition 2.4.1: the Emerton–Gee stack of weight-0 crystalline representations
items.statement: Let 𝒳_d be the Emerton–Gee stack of rank-d étale (φ, Γ)-modules for K [EG23 Def. 3.2.1] and 𝒳_d^{crys,0} = 𝒳^{crys,λ,τ}_{K,d} with λ_{σ,i} = d − i and τ trivial [EG23 Def. 4.8.8]. (1) 𝒳_d^{crys,0} is a p-adic formal algebraic stack, flat and of finite type over Spf O; its special fibre 𝒳̄_d^{crys,0} is algebraic. (2) For A° finite flat over O, 𝒳_d^{crys,0}(A°) consists of the G_K-representations that are crystalline of weight 0 after inverting p. (3) 𝒳̄_d^{crys,0} is equidimensional of dimension [K : ℚ_p]d(d − 1)/2. (4) For every point x : Spec 𝔽′ → 𝒳̄_d^{crys,0} there is a versal morphism Spf R^{crys,0,O′}_{ρ̄} → 𝒳_d^{crys,0} at x.
items.note: Imported from [EG23 Thm. 4.8.12, Thm. 4.8.14, Prop. 4.8.10]; the Emerton–Gee stacks are not planned in the atlas (EG23 is a prerequisite). Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings.

items.name: Serre weights, fundamental characters and maximally nonsplit representations of niveau one
items.statement: A Serre weight k is a tuple {k_{σ,i}}_{σ : k ↪ 𝔽̄_p, 1 ≤ i ≤ d} with p − 1 ≥ k_{σ,i} − k_{σ,i+1} ≥ 0 and p − 1 ≥ k_{σ,d} ≥ 0, not all k_{σ,d} = p − 1. ω_σ is the fundamental character I_K → O_K^× → k^× → 𝔽^× via σ; one chooses ω_{k,i} : G_K → 𝔽^× with ω_{k,i}|_{I_K} = Π_σ ω_σ^{−k_{σ,i}}, such that k_{σ,i} − k_{σ,i+1} = p − 1 for all σ forces ω_{k,i} = ω_{k,i+1}; ur_ν is the unramified character sending a geometric Frobenius to ν (printed 'to λ', sourceIssues E3). (G_m)^d_k is the torus of tuples (x_i) with x_i = x_{i+1} whenever k_{σ,i} − k_{σ,i+1} = p − 1 for all σ (p. 26). ρ̄ is maximally nonsplit of niveau one if it has a unique filtration with one-dimensional graded pieces; it has weight k if it is upper triangular as in (2.4.2) with diagonal ur_{ν_d}ω_{k,d}, ur_{ν_{d−1}}ε̄^{−1}ω_{k,d−1}, …, ur_{ν_1}ε̄^{1−d}ω_{k,1}. When ω_{k,i} = ω_{k,i+1}, k_{σ,i} − k_{σ,i+1} = p − 1 for all σ (printed with indices d − i, d + 1 − i; sourceIssues E4) exactly when ν_i = ν_{i+1} and the extension class in H¹(G_K, ε̄) is très ramifiée.
items.note: From [EG23 §5.5] as corrected in the errata [EG] (the paper notes that EG23 §5.5 erroneously claimed further constraints on the ω_{k,i}). FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.5 plans only the rank-2 residual types. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the definition of (G_m)^d_k (p. 26) was added.

items.name: Theorem 2.4.3: the irreducible components of 𝒳_{d,red}
items.statement: (1) 𝒳_{d,red} is an algebraic stack of finite presentation over 𝔽. (2) It is equidimensional of dimension [K : ℚ_p]d(d − 1)/2. (3) Its irreducible components are the 𝒳^k_{d,red}, indexed by Serre weights k, each containing a dense open 𝒰_k all of whose 𝔽̄_p-points are maximally nonsplit of niveau one and weight k. (4) There is a dense (equivalently nonempty) open T ⊂ (G_m)^d_k such that for all (t_1, …, t_d) ∈ T(𝔽̄_p) some 𝔽̄_p-point of 𝒰_k corresponds to a representation (2.4.2) with ν_i = t_i that is generic in the sense of Definition 2.3.1.
items.note: (1)–(3) are [EG23 Thm. 5.5.12, Thm. 6.5.1]; (4) follows from the corrected [EG23 Thm. 5.5.12] of [EG] and a cup-product argument (with help from M. Emerton, per the acknowledgements). Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): as printed, (4) is vacuous (T = ∅ satisfies it); the proof of Theorem 2.5.2 needs T nonempty and dense, which requires the eigenvalue morphism 𝒰^k → (G_m)^d_k to be dominant (sourceIssues E18). The cup-product step of the proof has a small gap (E19).

items.name: Theorem 2.5.2: the weight-0 Breuil–Mézard cycle, and generic reducedness of the special fibre of the stack
items.statement: Suppose p > d. Then Z_{crys,0} = 𝒳^0_{d,red}, where Z_{crys,0} = Σ_k μ_k 𝒳^k_{d,red} is the cycle of 𝒳̄_d^{crys,0} (2.5.1) and 0 is the Serre weight with all k_{σ,i} = 0. In particular 𝒳̄_d^{crys,0} is generically reduced.
items.locator: §2.5, (2.5.1), Theorem 2.5.2 and proof, pp. 27–28; Remark 2.5.4, p. 29
items.note: Proof: by Corollary 2.3.3 only k = 0 occurs; at a generic point of 𝒰_0 satisfying (2.5.3) the lifting ring is the ordinary crystalline ring of [CHT08 2.4.2], formally smooth [CHT08 Lem. 2.4.7], using Proposition 2.4.1(4) (printed 'Theorem 2.4.1', sourceIssues E5) and [Sta13 0DR0, 00MC, 033F, 04YH]. Remark 2.5.4: this computes the cycle Z_0 of the geometric Breuil–Mézard conjecture [EG23 Conj. 8.2.2] for p > d. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the paper writes Z_{crys,0}.

items.name: Theorem D (Theorem 2.5.5): generic reducedness of weight-0 crystalline lifting rings
items.statement: Suppose p > d, K/ℚ_p finite and E/ℚ_p finite containing the Galois closure of K, with ring of integers O, uniformiser ϖ and residue field 𝔽. Then for every ρ̄ : G_K → GL_d(𝔽), the special fibre R^{crys,0,O}_{ρ̄}/ϖ of the weight-0 crystalline lifting ring is generically reduced.
items.locator: §1, Theorem D, p. 8; §2.5, Theorem 2.5.5 and proof, p. 29
items.note: Proof as in [CEGS22a Thm. 4.6]: a smooth chart V → 𝒳̄_d^{crys,0} with Ô_{V,v} ≅ R^{crys,0,O}_{ρ̄}/ϖ [Sta13 0DR0]; the reduced dense open of Theorem 2.5.2 pulls back to a dense reduced open [Sta13 0CMK]; complete local rings of generically reduced finite-type schemes are generically reduced [CEGS22a Lem. 4.5]. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings.

items.name: Remarks 2.5.6–2.5.7: comparison with d = 2 and sharpness
items.statement: For d = 2, Theorem 2.5.5 is a case of [CEGS22a Thm. 4.6], proved there through the Kisin resolution. The Breuil–Mézard conjecture implies that the analogous statement fails for potentially crystalline weight-0 rings of generic tame type when d ≥ 4 (Breuil–Mézard multiplicities > 1 [LLHLM23 Rem. 8.1.4]), and that for parallel Serre weights k > 0 the special fibres of 𝒳_d^{crys,k} are not generically reduced once K is sufficiently ramified; an unconditional proof of the latter is 'presumably possible' by patching. The authors expect Theorem 2.5.2 to hold for p ≤ d as well.
items.note: Context for the brief (what the Part II must not claim). Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): material correction: both failure statements are conditional on the Breuil–Mézard conjecture (p. 29), not facts.

items.name: Decomposed generic residual representations
items.statement: ρ̄ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽̄_p) is decomposed generic [ACC+ Def. 4.3.1] if there is a prime l ≠ p splitting completely in F such that for every v | l, ρ̄ is unramified at v and the eigenvalues α_1, …, α_n of ρ̄(Frob_v) satisfy α_i/α_j ≠ l for i ≠ j.
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.7 (decomposed-generic API), as for PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Adequate subgroups
items.statement: Adequacy of a subgroup H ⊂ GL_n(𝔽) in the sense cited from [MT23, Definition 1.1.1] ('see, for example'): H acts absolutely irreducibly on 𝔽^n, H¹(H, 𝔽) = 0, H¹(H, ad) = 0, and End(𝔽^n) is spanned by the semisimple elements of H (Thorne's condition).
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 plans adequacy and the strengthened image conditions. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): stated in the standard form; the paper only cites [MT23, Definition 1.1.1].

items.name: Local deformation problems D^□_v, D^{crys,0}_v and D^χ_v
items.statement: A local deformation problem is a P̂GL_n-stable subfunctor of D^□_v = D^{□,O}_{ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}}} represented by a quotient R_v of R^□_v [ACC+ §6.2.1]. Used: D^□_v itself; for v | p the weight-0 crystalline lifts D^{crys,0}_v (R^{crys,0,O}); and D^χ_v [ACC+ §6.2.15] for q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial, p > n, and characters χ_i : O_{F_v}^× → O^× trivial mod ϖ: lifts with char ρ(σ)(X) = Π_i (X − χ_i(Art^{−1}_{F_v}(σ))) for σ ∈ I_{F_v}; with the component properties of [ACC+ Props. 6.2.16, 6.2.17].
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 constructs rank-n local conditions away from p and exports the component input used in ACC+ §6.2.

items.name: Global deformation problems and framed global deformation rings
items.statement: S = (ρ̄, S, {O}_{v∈S}, {D_v}_{v∈S}), S containing S_p and all places where ρ̄ is ramified, as in [ACC+ Def. 6.2.2] with Λ_v = O; D_S is represented by R_S, T-framed deformations by R^T_S, which receives R^{T,loc}_S = ⊗̂_{v∈T} R_v.
items.note: GlobalGaloisDeformations G8 (ACC+ Definition 6.2.2). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the condition on S (p. 30) was added.

items.name: Locally symmetric spaces X_K, Hecke algebras T^S(K, V) and the Hecke polynomial P_v(X)
items.statement: For F imaginary CM and a good (neat, compact open, factorisable) K ⊂ GL_n(𝔸_F^∞), X_K = GL_n(F)\(X_∞ × GL_n(𝔸_F^∞)/K) with X_∞ = GL_n(F_∞)/ℝ_{>0}K_∞. A finite O-module V with G(F) × K_S-action gives a local system on X_K and an action of H(GL_n(𝔸_F^{∞,S}), K^S) ⊗ O on RΓ(X_K, V) [ACC+ §2.1.2]; its image is T^S(K, V). P_v(X) = X^n − T_{v,1}X^{n−1} + ⋯ + (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{v,i}X^{n−i} + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_v^{n(n−1)/2}T_{v,n}, with T_{v,i} the double coset of diag(ϖ_v (i times), 1, …, 1).
items.note: ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0, ALS.1, ALS.3 (spaces, local systems, Hecke correspondences on complexes); IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2 (Hecke algebras on complexes) and IHG.3 (the integral spherical normalisation of T_{v,i} and P_v). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the item silently corrects a misprint: the paper prints the last term of P_v(X) as + q_v^{n(n−1)/2}T_{v,n}; it should be (−1)^n q_v^{n(n−1)/2}T_{v,n} (sourceIssues E20).

items.name: Galois representations attached to maximal ideals of T^S(K, V)
items.statement: If 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, V) is maximal there is a semisimple ρ̄_𝔪 : G_{F,S′} → GL_n(k(𝔪)) with char ρ̄_𝔪(Frob_v) equal to the image of P_v(X) for v ∉ S′ [ACC+ Thm. 2.3.5].
items.note: The torsion Galois determinants through nilpotent descent: TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.4 and IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.5.

items.name: Cohomology localised at non-Eisenstein 𝔪 is described by regular algebraic cuspidal representations of weight 0
items.statement: If ρ̄_𝔪 is absolutely irreducible, H^i(X_K, O)_𝔪 ⊗_O E is described in terms of cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n(𝔸_F) that are regular algebraic of weight 0 (π_∞ has the infinitesimal character of the trivial representation) [ACC+ Thm. 2.4.10].
items.note: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.5 (weighted cohomology and the automorphic comparison); regular algebraic weights in AG2.0.

items.name: The relation 'connects' (∼) of BLGGT14
items.statement: Continuous ρ_1, ρ_2 : G_K → GL_n(O_{ℚ̄_l}) connect, ρ_1 ∼ ρ_2 [BLGGT14 §1.4], if they have equivalent reductions, are potentially crystalline with the same labelled Hodge–Tate weights, and define points of the same irreducible component of the corresponding lifting ring over ℚ̄_l (for weight 0 crystalline: of R^{crys,0,O}_{ρ̄} ⊗_O ℚ̄_p, Remark 3.2.2). It is compatible with restriction, direct sums and tensor products ([BLGGT14 p. 530 (5)]).
items.locator: §3.2, Theorem 3.2.1(5c) and Remark 3.2.2, pp. 31–32; proof of Proposition 6.2.3, p. 56
items.note: Routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (components of potentially semistable lifting rings), as PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25 routed its own 'connects' item.

items.name: Caraiani–Newton local–global compatibility at p in weight 0
items.statement: For π regular algebraic cuspidal of weight 0 on GL_n(𝔸_F), F imaginary CM, with π_v unramified at v | p, r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is crystalline with the same labelled Hodge–Tate weights {0, …, n − 1} [CN23 Thm. 4.3.1]; the torsion version [CN23 Thm. 4.2.15] shows that the Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations satisfy the crystalline weight-0 local condition at v | p, with arbitrary ramification of p in F.
items.locator: §3.1, p. 30; Remark 3.2.2, Proposition 3.2.3 and proof of Theorem 3.2.5, pp. 32–34
items.note: Imported from Caraiani–Newton (arXiv 2301.10509), a prerequisite; the atlas plans local–global compatibility at p only in the Fontaine–Laffaille and ordinary cases (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.1, PA.2). Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): Remark 3.2.2 applies [CN23, Thm. 4.3.1] under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.2.1 with F imaginary CM and r̄_ι(π) decomposed generic; the totally real case of Theorem 3.2.1 needs a base change step the paper does not state.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.1: automorphy lifting in weight 0 with p arbitrarily ramified
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field and p > n prime. Let ρ : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) be continuous with (1) ρ unramified almost everywhere; (2) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} crystalline of weight 0 for every v | p; (3) ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, with ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} of adequate image; (4) some σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar; (5) a cuspidal π of GL_n(𝔸_F), regular algebraic of weight 0, with ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π) and, for v | p, π_v unramified and r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ ρ|_{G_{F_v}}. Then ρ is automorphic: ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for a cuspidal Π of weight 0, and Π_v is unramified whenever v | p or both ρ and π are unramified at v.
items.note: A version of [ACC+ Thm. 6.1.1] and [MT23 Thm. 1.2] allowing arbitrary ramification at p in weight 0. Deduced from Theorem 3.2.5 by the base change argument of [ACC+ §6.5.12]. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: The setting of §3.2: hypotheses (1)–(8), the level K and the problems S_χ
items.statement: F imaginary CM with maximal totally real F⁺, p > n odd, π cuspidal regular algebraic of weight 0, S ⊇ S_p and R ⊂ S − S_p with: (1) every prime below S or ramified in F splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F; (2) for each v ∈ S_p there is a place v̄′ ≠ v̄ of F⁺ above p with Σ_{v̄″|p, v̄″≠v̄,v̄′}[F⁺_{v̄″} : ℚ_p] > ½[F⁺ : ℚ_p]; (3) r̄_ι(π) absolutely irreducible, decomposed generic, adequate on G_{F(ζ_p)}; (4) π_v unramified for v | p; (5) for v ∈ R, π_v^{Iw_v} ≠ 0, q_v ≡ 1 mod p, r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} trivial; (6) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p), π_v unramified, v ∉ R^c, H²(F_v, ad r̄_ι(π)) = 0; (7) two places of S − (R ∪ S_p) of distinct residue characteristics; (8) π unramified outside S. K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) (v ∉ S or v | p), Iw_v (v ∈ R), Iw_{v,1} (otherwise); 𝔪 with ρ̄_𝔪 ≅ r̄_ι(π); S_χ = (ρ̄_𝔪, S, {O}, {D^{crys,0}_v}_{S_p} ∪ {D^χ_v}_R ∪ {D^□_v}_{S−(R∪S_p)}), with χ_{v,i} : k(v)^× → O^× trivial mod ϖ, and trivial or pairwise distinct at each v ∈ R, and the module O(χ^{−1}).
items.note: Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): condition (2) and the characters χ_{v,i} were stated as printed (pp. 32–33).

items.name: Proposition 3.2.3: Galois representations valued in the Hecke algebra with the crystalline condition
items.statement: There are δ ≥ 1 depending only on n and [F : ℚ], an ideal J ⊂ T^S(RΓ(X_K, O(χ^{−1})))_𝔪 with J^δ = 0, and a continuous surjection f_{S_χ} : R_{S_χ} → T^S(RΓ(X_K, O(χ^{−1})))_𝔪/J such that char(f_{S_χ} ∘ ρ_{S_χ}(Frob_v)) is the image of P_v(X) for every finite v ∉ S.
items.note: A version of [ACC+ Prop. 6.5.3], using [CN23 Thm. 4.2.15] for the condition at v ∈ S_p. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.4: the completed tensor products of local deformation rings
items.statement: Fix χ trivial, or pairwise distinct at each v ∈ R. (1) R^{S,loc}_{S_χ} is equidimensional of dimension 1 + n²|S| + (n(n − 1)/2)[F : ℚ], with every generic point of characteristic 0. (2) Every generic point of Spec R^{S,loc}_{S_χ}/ϖ specialises from a unique generic point of Spec R^{S,loc}_{S_χ}. (3) If the χ_{v,i} are pairwise distinct, Spec R^{S,loc}_{S_χ} → Spec R^{S_p,loc}_{S_χ} = Spec R^{S_p,loc}_{S_1} is a bijection on irreducible components. (4) Each characteristic-zero point of Spec R^{S_p,loc}_{S_1} lies on a unique irreducible component. (5) With χ pairwise distinct and C a component of Spec R^{S,loc}_{S_1} with image C_p, the generic points of C ∩ Spec R^{S,loc}_{S_1}/ϖ generalise to the generic point of Spec R^{S,loc}_{S_χ} corresponding to C_p.
items.note: Inputs: [BLGHT11 Lem. 3.3], [ACC+ Lem. 6.2.25, Props. 6.2.16–6.2.17], [Kis08 Thms. 3.3.4, 3.3.8], and Theorem 2.5.5 with [CN23 Lem. 5.3.3] (generically reduced special fibre ⇒ unique generalisations). Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: Generic reducedness of the special fibre implies unique generalisation of its generic points
items.statement: If R is a complete local Noetherian O-flat ring whose special fibre R/ϖ is generically reduced, then every generic point of Spec R/ϖ is the specialisation of a unique generic point of Spec R [CN23 Lem. 5.3.3].
items.note: The bridge from Theorem D to derived Ihara avoidance. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: Theorem 3.2.5: change of the component at p preserves support (derived Ihara avoidance)
items.statement: Let f_1, f_2 : R_{S_1} → O have associated lifts ρ_1, ρ_2 : G_{F,S} → GL_n(O). If ker(f_1) ∈ Supp_{R_{S_1}}(H*(X_K, O)_𝔪) and ρ_1|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ ρ_2|_{G_{F_v}} for each v ∈ S_p, then ker(f_2) ∈ Supp_{R_{S_1}}(H*(X_K, O)_𝔪).
items.note: Calegari–Geraghty patching as in [ACC+ §§6.4–6.5] and [MT23 §8] with the crystalline weight-0 condition at p; the support argument uses [CN23 Prop. 5.4.2, Cor. 5.4.3] and Lemma 3.2.4. PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.3–PA.4 and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8–P9 plan the generic patching and support machinery; this weight-0 instance is routed to WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: The patched objects in weight 0
items.statement: Patching supplies: S_∞ = O[[X_1, …, X_r]] with augmentation ideal 𝔞_∞; perfect complexes C_∞, C′_∞ of S_∞-modules with C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ ≅ C′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ and C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/𝔞_∞ ≅ RHom_O(RΓ(X_K, O)_𝔪, O)[−d]; S_∞-subalgebras T_∞, T′_∞ with common image modulo ϖ, T_∞ → T(K, O)_𝔪; complete local S_∞-algebras R_∞, R′_∞, power series over R^{S,loc}_{S_1}, R^{S,loc}_{S_χ}, with R_∞ ↠ T_∞/I_∞, R′_∞ ↠ T′_∞/I′_∞ (nilpotent I) and a commutative square to R_{S_1} → T(K, O)^red_𝔪; R_∞/ϖ ≅ R′_∞/ϖ compatibly; and q_0, l_0 with H*(X_K, E)_𝔪 ≠ 0 exactly in [q_0, q_0 + l_0] and dim R_∞ = dim R′_∞ = dim S_∞ − l_0.
items.note: ACC+ §§6.4–6.5 with the weight-0 crystalline condition at p. Routed to WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: Ordinary automorphy lifting with adequate image (Miagkov–Thorne)
items.statement: [MT23 Thm. 1.3]: an ordinary analogue of Theorem 3.2.1 over CM fields with adequate (rather than enormous) residual image; its conclusion includes that the automorphic representation is unramified at every place where both the Galois representation of the given automorphic representation and the lifted representation are unramified.
items.note: Used to show S_UA weakly automorphic from the automorphy of Sym^{nm−1} of an elliptic curve. Imported (MT23 is a prerequisite); routed to WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting with the other ACC+-style lifting theorems of the paper. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): corrected against p. 60: both representations are characteristic-zero ones.

items.name: The Dwork family and the character χ
items.statement: Let n > 2 and N > 100n + 100 be integers, N odd and (N, n) = 1. Over T_0 = Spec R_0[t, (1 − t^N)^{−1}], R_0 = ℤ[ζ_N, N^{−1}], let Z ⊂ ℙ^{N−1}_{T_0} be X_1^N + ⋯ + X_N^N = NtX_1⋯X_N, smooth of degree N and dimension N − 2, π : Z → T_0. H = μ_N^N/Δ(μ_N) acts on ℙ^{N−1}; H_0 = ker(Π : H → μ_N) preserves Z, and H acts on the Fermat fibre Z_0. With M = ℚ(e^{2πi/N}), X = Hom(H, M^×) ≅ ker(Σ : (ℤ/Nℤ)^N → ℤ/Nℤ) (via a choice of τ). Choose χ = (χ_1, …, χ_N) ∈ X (printed 'χ ∈ (χ_1, …, χ_N)', sourceIssues E6) in which the trivial character occurs n + 1 times and every other at most once, such that the stabiliser in Gal(M/ℚ) of the set {ρ_1, …, ρ_n} of missing nontrivial characters is trivial; it exists by [Qia23 Lem. 3.1].
items.note: Qian's non-self-dual Dwork motives. Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII (PAPER-QIAN-23), which owns this family.

items.name: The eigensheaves V_λ and their stalks
items.statement: For a place λ of M of characteristic l, V_λ = (R^{N−2}π[1/l]_* O_{M_λ})^{H_0 = χ|_{H_0}} (printed with π_*), a lisse sheaf of finite free O_{M_λ}-modules on T_0[1/l]; V_{t,λ} is its stalk at a geometric point over t ∈ T_0(k).
items.note: Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII.

items.name: Katz's hypergeometric sheaf E_λ
items.statement: On T_1 = Spec R_0[t, t^{−1}, (1 − t)^{−1}], with j : T_1 → G_{m,R_0} the open immersion and f : t ↦ 1 − t, L_i the rank-one sheaf of ρ_i and the Kummer μ_N-torsor, F_i = j[1/l]_! f[1/l]^* L_i, set E_λ = j[1/l]^*(F_1 ∗_! F_2 ∗_! ⋯ ∗_! F_n)[n − 1], the restriction to T_1[1/l] of the shifted multiplicative convolution with compact support on G_{m,R_0}[1/l] [Kat90 Ch. 8, Kat09].
items.note: Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): material correction: the paper applies j^* (pullback), not j_*; the convolution lives on G_m and is restricted to T_1 (p. 36, page image).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1: properties of E_λ and comparison with the Dwork family
items.statement: (1) E_λ is lisse of rank n on T_1[1/l], geometrically irreducible after ⊗ M̄_λ, pure of weight n − 1, with det E_λ ≅ M_λ(n(1 − n)/2). (2) For x ∈ T_1(k), k finite with q elements, tr(Frob_k | E_{λ,x}) = (−1)^{n−1} Σ_{x_1⋯x_n = x} Π_i ρ_i((1 − x_i)^{(q−1)/N}) (4.2.2), with ρ_i(0) = 0. (3) There is a unique character Ψ_λ of π_1(Spec R_0[1/l]) such that, with g : T′_0 = T_0[1/t] → T_1, t ↦ t^{−N}, (j′)^*V_λ ⊗_{O_{M_λ}} M_λ ≅ g^*E_λ ⊗_{M_λ} M_λ(Ψ_λ) (4.2.3), with Ψ_λ valued in O_{M_λ}^×.
items.note: From [Kat09], [Kat90 Ch. 8, Thm. 8.12.2(1a)], [DK17 §A.1.6] and [Kat09 Thm. 5.3]. Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): (4.2.3) is printed over M_λ. V_λ is defined on p. 36 as (π[1/l]_*O_{M_λ})^{H_0=χ}, which should be R^{N−2}π[1/l]_* (sourceIssues E21).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.4: the twisting character Ψ comes from an algebraic Hecke character
items.statement: There is a Hecke character Ψ : ℚ(ζ_N)^×\𝔸^×_{ℚ(ζ_N)} → ℂ^× of type A_0, unramified away from N, defined over M, with Ψ_λ associated to Ψ for every λ; and Ψ·c(Ψ) corresponds to ε^{n+1−N} (printed Ψc(Ψ) = |·|^{N−n}; sourceIssues E7), i.e. Ψ has weight N − n − 1.
items.note: Proof: λ-independence of Frobenius traces as in [Kat09 Question 5.5], Henniart's theorem [Hen82], and c-linear isomorphisms V_{c(λ)} ≅ V_λ^∨(2 − N) (printed (1 − N)) and E_{c(λ)} ≅ E_λ^∨(1 − n) with Schur's lemma.  Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the magnitude N − n − 1 is forced by weights and Hodge numbers; the sign is stated without a normalisation (the paper's Art is geometric). The note's pointer to ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity CM.4 was removed: CM.4 concerns CM abelian varieties, and Henniart's theorem is now item 127.

items.name: The twisted local systems W_λ
items.statement: W_λ = V_λ ⊗ O_{M_λ}(Ψ_λ^{−1}): W_λ ⊗ M_λ is lisse of rank n, pure of weight n − 1, geometrically irreducible, with determinant M_λ(n(1 − n)/2); W_{t,λ} is the stalk at t and W̄_λ = W_λ ⊗ k(λ).
items.note: Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII.

items.name: Katz–Messing: independence of ℓ for Frobenius twisted by automorphisms
items.statement: For a smooth proper variety over a finite field with an action of a finite group H, the characteristic polynomial of h·Frob on H^i_ét(−, ℚ̄_λ) has coefficients in O_M independent of λ ∤ char, and agrees with that on crystalline cohomology [KM74 Thm. 2(2)], applicable to crystalline cohomology by [GM87].
items.note: Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.5: the compatible system W_{t,λ}
items.statement: Let F/ℚ(ζ_N) be a number field. (1) If v has residue characteristic l′ ∤ N, λ has residue characteristic ≠ l′, and t ∈ T_0(O_{F_v}), W_{t,λ} is unramified at v and Q_v(X) = det(X − Frob_v | W_{t,λ}) ∈ O_M[X] is independent of λ. (2) If char v = char λ = l and t ∈ T_0(F_v), W_{t,λ} is de Rham with HT_τ(W_{t,λ}) = {0, 1, …, n − 1}; if moreover l ∤ N and t ∈ T_0(O_{F_v}), it is crystalline, Frob_v on WD(W_{t,λ}) has characteristic polynomial Q_v(X), and W_{t,λ} is ordinary iff the roots of Q_v have l-adic valuations 0, [k(v) : 𝔽_l], …, (n − 1)[k(v) : 𝔽_l]. (3) For t ∈ T_0(F) and S the places dividing N or where t is not integral, (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {W^ss_{t,λ}}, {{0, …, n − 1}}) is a weakly compatible system of rank n, pure of weight n − 1 [BLGGT14 §5.1].
items.note: Uses smooth proper base change, [KM74], the crystalline comparison (CohomologyComparisons CP.2) with [GM87], [Qia23 Lem. 3.10] and [Ger19 Lem. 2.32]. Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): part (1) restated; its proof deduces integrality of Q_v from that of the untwisted polynomial, which does not transfer through the Ψ-twist (sourceIssues E24); integrality holds by a different argument.

items.name: Drinfeld–Kedlaya: generic slopes of indecomposable F-isocrystals
items.statement: [DK17 Thm. 1.3.3]: applied by the paper to the lisse λ′-adic sheaf W_{λ′} (char λ′ ≠ l) on a smooth irreducible variety over a finite field, with algebraic Frobenius polynomials, measuring λ-adic slopes, there is a nonempty open on which the generic Newton slopes s_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ s_n are constant and satisfy s_i ≤ s_{i+1} + 1.
items.note: Imported (DK17 is a prerequisite). Overconvergent F-isocrystals are planned in PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.3, the slope theorem is not. Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): restated as the paper applies it (p. 38).

items.name: Proposition 4.2.6: generic crystalline ordinarity of the Dwork family
items.statement: Let v be a place of ℚ(ζ_N) of characteristic l ∤ N and λ a place of M of the same characteristic. There is a nonempty Zariski open U(v; λ) ⊂ T_{0,k(v)} such that for every finite F_w/ℚ(ζ_N)_v and every t ∈ T_0(O_{F_w}) reducing into U(v; λ)(k(w)), W_{t,λ} is a crystalline ordinary representation of G_{F_w}.
items.note: Proof: by Drinfeld–Kedlaya and the determinant it suffices that s_n(x) = 0 generically; by (4.2.3) and (4.2.2) this reduces to tr(Frob_x | E_{μ,x}) ≢ 0 mod λ off the zeros of u(T) = Σ_r (−1)^{nr} Π_i C(c_i, r) T^r, via the norm identity N_{k/k(v)}(u(x)) = Σ_r (−1)^{nr} Π_i C(c̃_i, r) x^r (sourceIssues E8 in one exponent). Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII.

items.name: Power sums over the units of a finite field
items.statement: For a finite field of cardinality q, Σ_{z ∈ k^×} z^r = 0 unless (q − 1) | r (then it is −1).
items.note: Used to collapse the character sum.

items.name: Lucas's congruence for binomial coefficients
items.statement: For a prime l, C(n, k) ≡ Π_i C(n_i, k_i) mod l where n_i, k_i are the base-l digits; iterating gives the base-q_v form C(c̃_i, r) ≡ Π_j C(c_i, r_j) mod l used in the proof (from (1 + X)^{c̃_i} = Π_j (1 + X^{q_v^j})^{c_i} in 𝔽_l[X]).
items.note: Mathlib's Lucas theorem (with the mixed-radix form).

items.name: Definitions 4.3.1–4.3.2: finite unitary groups and Hermitian forms
items.statement: For a quadratic extension l/k of finite fields with Galois generator c and M† = (M^c)^t, GU_n(l) = {M ∈ GL_n(l) : M†M = λ ∈ k^×}, with multiplier ν(M) = M†M and SU_n(l) = ker ν. A Hermitian form on an l-space V is k-bilinear with ⟨ax, y⟩ = a⟨x, y⟩, ⟨x, ay⟩ = c(a)⟨x, y⟩ and ⟨y, x⟩ = c⟨x, y⟩; scaling by η with cη = −η gives the skew version (Remark 4.3.3).
items.note: Routed with the Dwork monodromy it serves (Proposition 4.4.2, Remark 4.4.3). Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.4: conjugate-self-dual absolutely irreducible representations are unitary
items.statement: Let V be an l-vector space with an absolutely irreducible representation of a group G and an l-linear isomorphism V^∨ ≅ V^c ⊗ χ^{−1} (4.3.4) for some χ : G → k^×. Then in a suitable basis G → GL_n(l) has image in GU_n(l) (with multiplier χ).
items.note: Proof by Schur's lemma, Hilbert 90 and the uniqueness of nondegenerate Hermitian forms over finite fields [Lew82 §4]. Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII.

items.name: Hilbert's Theorem 90 for a cyclic extension
items.statement: If L/K is a finite cyclic Galois extension with generator g and N_{L/K}(x) = 1, then x = y/g(y) for some y ∈ L^×.
items.note: Used for λ = c(η)/η.

items.name: Definition 4.4.1: the moduli spaces T({U_{λ_i}}) of level structures on W̄
items.statement: For distinct primes l_1, l_2 ∤ 2N, places λ_i of M above them and data (1) étale sheaves U_{λ_i} of rank-n k(λ_i)-modules on Spec F, (2) isomorphisms η_i : ∧^n W̄_{λ_i} → ∧^n U_{λ_i}, (3) when −1 mod N ∈ ⟨l_i⟩ a perfect 𝔽_{l_i}-bilinear pairing U × U → k(λ_i)(1 − n) that is Hermitian up to η with cη = −η (the Dwork side has the matching pairing from Poincaré duality), the functor F({U_{λ_i}}) of pairs of isomorphisms φ_i : W̄_{λ_i,S} → U_{λ_i,S} with ∧^n φ_i = η_i and preserving the pairings is represented by a finite étale T_{0,F}-scheme T({U_{λ_i}}).
items.note: New relative to Qian: the unitary case −1 mod N ∈ ⟨l⟩ is allowed. Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): λ_i are places of M (printed 'of ℚ(ζ_N)', sourceIssues E22) and the pairing is 𝔽_{l_i}-bilinear. The data do not require η_i to be compatible with the pairings induced on ∧^n, so the functor can be empty (sourceIssues E23).

items.name: Proposition 4.4.2: T({U_{λ_i}}) is geometrically irreducible
items.statement: With notation as above, T({U_{λ_i}}) is a geometrically irreducible smooth F-scheme, provided (in the unitary case) η_i is compatible with the pairings induced on ∧^n (otherwise it can be empty).
items.note: Proof: the geometric monodromy of W̄_{λ_i} is SU_n(k(λ_i)) when −1 mod N ∈ ⟨l_i⟩ (a variant of [Qia23 Lem. 3.7]: a subgroup of index dividing N, coprime to n) and SL_n(k(λ_i)) otherwise; Lemma 5.2.3 and Goursat's lemma give the product. Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the compatibility proviso was added (sourceIssues E23).

items.name: Goursat's lemma
items.statement: A subgroup of G × H surjecting onto both factors is the preimage of the graph of an isomorphism G/G′ ≅ H/H′ for normal subgroups G′, H′.

items.name: Remark 4.4.3: the level-structure data as residual representations
items.statement: If l ≡ 1 mod N and λ | l, the data (1)–(3) amount to r̄_l : G_F → GL_n(𝔽_l) with determinant ε̄^{−n(n−1)/2}; if l ≡ −1 mod N, to r̄_l : G_F → GU_n(𝔽_{l²}) with multiplier ε̄^{1−n} (Lemma 4.3.4). For l_1, l_2 ≡ ±1 mod N one writes T(r̄_{λ_1}, r̄_{λ_2}), and T(r̄_λ) for one prime l ≡ 1 mod N; T(r̄_λ) is geometrically irreducible.
items.note: Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): subject to the same compatibility of η with the pairings (sourceIssues E23).

items.name: Lemma 4.4.4: the Fermat fibre at primes l ≡ −1 mod N
items.statement: Let l > n be prime with l ≡ −1 mod N, v, λ places of ℚ(ζ_N), M above l, τ, cτ : k(v) → k(λ) the two isomorphisms and ω_τ = τ ∘ Art^{−1} on inertia. Then W̄_{0,λ} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^n ω_τ^{i−1} ω_{cτ}^{n−i} as representations of I_{ℚ(ζ_N)_v}.
items.note: Proof: the H-eigenspace decomposition of the middle cohomology H^{N−2}(Z_{0,ℚ̄}) of the Fermat fibre (printed H^{N−1}; sourceIssues E9) into lines [DMOS82 I.7.4], orthogonal for the pairing. Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): ω_τ is defined only on inertia.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.1, first part: Moret-Bailly over CM fields with prescribed local points
items.statement: Let F be imaginary CM, Galois over ℚ, T/F smooth and geometrically irreducible; given F^avoid/F finite, a finite set S_0 of rational primes, for l ∈ S_0 and v | l Galois extensions L_v/F_v with σ(L_v) = L_{σ(v)} for σ ∈ G_{ℚ_l}, and nonempty Gal(L_v/F_v)-stable open Ω_v ⊂ T(L_v): there is a finite CM extension F′/F, Galois over ℚ and linearly disjoint from F^avoid, and P ∈ T(F′), such that F′_w ≅ L_v and P ∈ Ω_v for all w | v | l ∈ S_0.
items.locator: §4.5, Proposition 4.5.1 and first paragraph of proof, p. 43
items.note: A special case of [BLGGT14 Prop. 3.1.1] with F′ = FE, E totally real ([Cal12 Thm. 3.1]); PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1 plans Moret-Bailly with prescribed local opens, splitting and linear disjointness (as for PAPER-QIAN-23's item).

items.name: Proposition 4.5.1, last part: surjectivity onto a finite quotient of π_1
items.statement: Given further a finite group G and a surjection f : π_1^ét(T) → G, the point P can be chosen so that f ∘ P_* : G_{F′} → G is surjective.
items.locator: §4.5, Proposition 4.5.1 and second paragraph of proof, pp. 43–44
items.note: Proof: spread T out over O_F and add local conditions at places of large norm, one per conjugacy class, from the Chebotarev density theorem for schemes of finite type [Ser12 Cor. 9.12]; Jordan's theorem gives surjectivity (cf. [Cal12 Prop. 3.2]). Routed as a source of PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1.

items.name: Definition 5.1.1: the representations ρ_{n,m,0}
items.statement: For n, m ≥ 1 let ε_2, ε′_2 : G_{ℚ_{p²}} → ℤ̄_p^× be the two Lubin–Tate characters trivial on Art(p), and ρ_{n,m,0} = ⊕_{i=1}^n ε_2^{m(n−i)}(ε′_2)^{m(i−1)} : G_{ℚ_{p²}} → GL_n(ℤ̄_p), with Hodge–Tate weights {0, m, …, (n − 1)m} at each embedding (so ρ_{n,1,0} has weight 0 and ε_2ε′_2 = ε^{−1}); the paper assumes p > nm, so it is Fontaine–Laffaille; ρ_0 = ρ_{n,1,0}.
items.note: Level-2 fundamental characters are planned in ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.2; this local model is routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 with the connectedness lemmas. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the Hodge–Tate normalisation actually used and the standing hypothesis p > nm were made explicit.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.3: crystalline lifts of ρ̄_{n,m,0} connect to ρ_{n,m,0}
items.statement: Assume p > nm. Let K_0/ℚ_{p²} be unramified and ρ : G_{K_0} → GL_n(ℤ̄_p) crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights {0, m, …, (n − 1)m} and ρ̄|_{I_{K_0}} = ρ̄_{n,m,0}|_{I_{K_0}}. Then (1) ρ̄|_{G_{K_1}} = ρ̄_{n,m,0}|_{G_{K_1}} for some finite unramified K_1/K_0; (2) for every finite K/K_0 with ρ̄|_{G_K} = ρ̄_{n,m,0}|_{G_K}, ρ|_{G_K} ∼ ρ_{n,m,0}|_{G_K}.
items.note: Proof: the Fontaine–Laffaille lifting ring is formally smooth (p > nm), planned in L7. Routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the standing hypothesis p > nm of Definition 5.1.1 was added. The proof prints ρ_0 where ρ_{n,m,0} is meant (sourceIssues E26).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.4: ordinary weight-0 crystalline lifts of the trivial representation connect
items.statement: If ρ_1, ρ_2 are ordinary crystalline weight-0 representations of G_K with ρ̄_1 = ρ̄_2 trivial, then ρ_1 ∼ ρ_2.
items.note: The ordinary weight-0 crystalline lifting ring of the trivial representation is irreducible [Ger19 Lem. 3.14]. Routed as a source of L7 (ordinary deformation functors and components).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.5: nearby weight-0 crystalline lifts lie on the same component
items.statement: Let ρ : G_K → GL_n(ℤ̄_p) be crystalline of weight 0. There is c = c(K, ρ, n) such that every crystalline weight-0 t : G_K → GL_n(ℤ̄_p) with t ≡ ρ mod p^c satisfies t ∼ ρ.
items.note: Proof: the generic fibre of the lifting ring is formally smooth at ρ [Kis08 Thm. 3.3.8], so ρ lies on a unique minimal prime; the finitely many other minimal primes contain elements with nonzero constant term. Routed as a source of L7.

items.name: Definition 5.2.1: the Taylor–Wiles big image conditions
items.statement: s̄ : G_F → GL_n(𝔽̄_p) satisfies the Taylor–Wiles big image conditions if (1) s̄ is decomposed generic, (2) s̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has adequate image, and (3) there is σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with s̄(σ) scalar.
items.note: The combination of hypotheses (3)–(4) of Theorem 3.2.1. Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4, G7).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.2: the big image conditions survive disjoint base change
items.statement: Let s̄ satisfy the Taylor–Wiles big image conditions, F/ℚ Galois, and H/F finite with Galois closure over ℚ linearly disjoint over F from the composite of F(ζ_p) and the Galois closure of the fixed field of ker s̄. Then s̄|_{G_H} satisfies the Taylor–Wiles big image conditions.
items.note: Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4, G7).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.3: simplicity and automorphisms of PSL_n and PSU_n over finite fields
items.statement: For G = PSL_n(𝔽_{p^k}) or PSU_n(𝔽_{p^{2k}}) (n ≥ 2): G is simple unless (n, p) ∈ {(2, 2), (2, 3), (3, 2)}; these groups are pairwise non-isomorphic except PSL_2(𝔽_{p^k}) ≅ PSU_2(𝔽_{p^{2k}}), PSL_2(𝔽_5) ≅ PSL_2(𝔽_4), PSL_2(𝔽_7) ≅ PSL_3(𝔽_2). For G = PSL_2(𝔽_{p^k}) or PSU_n(𝔽_{p^{2k}}) and A ∈ G the image of a matrix with eigenvalues in 𝔽_p, every automorphism of G preserves these eigenvalues up to scalar.
items.note: From [Ste68 Thm. 37], [Car72], [Ste60], [Car72 Thm. 12.5.1]. R01.4 consumes general finite-group classification results. Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4, G7).

items.name: Lemma 5.2.4: big image for Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B with r̄_B unitary
items.statement: Let F/ℚ be Galois, r̄_A : G_F → GL_2(𝔽_p) and r̄_B : G_F → GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) ⊂ GL_m(𝔽_{p²}) with r̄_A(G_{F(ζ_p)}) = SL_2(𝔽_p) and r̄_B(G_{F(ζ_p)}) = SU_m(𝔽_{p²}); let s̄ = Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B, p > 2mn + 1, and if m = 2 assume the projective kernel fields of r̄_A and r̄_B are linearly disjoint over F(ζ_p). (1) s̄ is decomposed generic and s̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has adequate image. (2) If det r̄_A = ε̄^{−m} and r̄_B has multiplier ε̄^{1−m}, then s̄ has image in GU_{mn}(𝔽_{p²}) with multiplier ε̄^{1−mn}. (3) If moreover ε̄(G_F) = 𝔽_p^×, s̄ satisfies the Taylor–Wiles big image conditions.
items.note: Proof via Chebotarev with Frobenius (A, …, A) × (B, …, B), [Tho12 Thm. A.9] and Lemma 4.3.4 (sourceIssues E10, E11 in the proof). Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4, G7). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): material correction: the representations are 𝔽_p- and 𝔽_{p²}-valued (p. 46), which the proof of (3) uses. For m = 2 the disjointness hypothesis is too weak for the proof (sourceIssues E31).

items.name: Absolutely irreducible images are adequate for large p
items.statement: [GHTT12 / Tho12, Thm. A.9]: an absolutely irreducible subgroup of GL_n(𝔽̄_p) is adequate when p ≥ 2(n + 1) (the paper uses p > 2mn + 1 and q > 2nm + 1).
items.locator: §5.2, proof of Lemma 5.2.4, p. 47; proof of Theorem 6.2.4, p. 60
items.note: Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7, which plans adequacy and its verification lemmas. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the exact bound was stated.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.5: Frobenius eigenvalues of an induced representation
items.statement: Let E/ℚ be cyclic of degree m, linearly disjoint from F, L = EF, ψ : G_L → 𝔽_p^× (p ∤ m) and r̄_B = Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ψ. If q splits completely in F, r̄_B is unramified above q and Frob_q generates Gal(E/ℚ), then for v | q the eigenvalues of r̄_B(Frob_v) are λ, ζλ, …, ζ^{m−1}λ with ζ a primitive m-th root of unity.
items.note: Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4, G7). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the character is 𝔽_p-valued (p. 47), and p ∤ m is needed.

items.name: Lemma 5.2.6: big image for Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B with r̄_B induced
items.statement: Let F/ℚ be Galois, r̄_A : G_F → GL_2(𝔽_p) with r̄_A(G_{F(ζ_p)}) = SL_2(𝔽_p), and r̄_B : G_F → GL_m(𝔽_p) with r̄_B ≅ Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} ψ for a character ψ : G_L → 𝔽_p^×, where E/ℚ is cyclic of degree m linearly disjoint from F and L = EF, and r̄_B|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} irreducible. Let s̄ = Sym^{n−1}r̄_A ⊗ r̄_B and p > 2mn + 1. (1) s̄ is decomposed generic with adequate image on G_{F(ζ_p)}. (2) If det r̄_A = ε̄^{−m}, det r̄_B = ε̄^{−m(m−1)/2} and ε̄(G_L) = 𝔽_p^×, s̄ satisfies the Taylor–Wiles big image conditions.
items.note: Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations (R01.4, G7). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): material correction: the coefficient fields are 𝔽_p (p. 48). As printed, (1) needs 'absolutely irreducible' in the hypothesis on r̄_B|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} (sourceIssues E28), and its proof must take α a square (E27).

items.name: Lemma 5.3.1: globalising local characters
items.statement: Let F be a number field, S a finite set of places containing no place above 2, and ψ_v : G_{F_v} → ℤ/nℤ for v ∈ S. Then there is χ : G_F → ℤ/nℤ with χ|_{G_{F_v}} = ψ_v for all v ∈ S.
items.note: From the Grunwald–Wang theorem [AT09 §X Thm. 5] ([Con11 App. A]); Tau Ceti's class field theory roadmap explicitly excludes Grunwald–Wang. Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality (R02.2, R02.4), as PAPER-QIAN-23 routed its character-root obstruction.

items.name: Remark 5.3.2: the Grunwald–Wang obstruction
items.statement: The hypothesis on S cannot be dropped (F = ℚ, v = 2, n = 8, ψ_2 unramified of order 8), and for general F one cannot even globalise ψ_v up to an unramified twist: for F = ℚ(√−5) there is ψ_2 : F_2^× → ℤ/8ℤ nontrivial on 16 with no global χ and unramified φ_2 such that χ_2 = ψ_2φ_2, since 16 is an 8th power at every odd place and at ∞ but not in F_2 ≅ ℚ_2(√−5).
items.note: The argument that 16 is not an 8th power in F_2 also needs −2 to be a nonsquare (sourceIssues E12). Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality.

items.name: Lemma 5.3.3: roots of finite-order characters after a totally real base change
items.statement: Let η be a finite-order character of G_F, F imaginary CM (totally imaginary), m an integer and F^avoid/F finite. There is a totally real Galois M/ℚ, linearly disjoint from F^avoid, and a character ψ of G_{MF} with η|_{G_{MF}} = ψ^m. If η is unramified above a finite set T of primes not containing 2, M can be taken totally split above T and ψ unramified above T.
items.note: Proof: reduce to m prime; the obstruction ∂η ∈ H²(F, ℤ/m) ↪ Br(F(ζ_m))[m] (Hochschild–Serre), Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether, local degree killing [CF86 §VI Thm. 3], [AT09 §X Thm. 6], [CHT08 Lem. 4.1.2], then Lemma 5.3.1. As in [ACC+ Thm. 7.1.11]. Routed as a source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality (R02.2, R02.4). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): material correction: the proof uses that F is totally imaginary (Br(ℂ) = 0), and the statement fails for totally real F (m = 2, η the character of F(i)/F).

items.name: Linear disjointness of field extensions
items.statement: The linear disjointness of intermediate fields and its characterisations used throughout (e.g. Lemma 5.2.2, Proposition 4.5.1, Theorem 6.2.4).
items.note: As cited by PAPER-QIAN-23.

items.name: Definition 6.1.1: very weakly compatible systems, restriction and tensor product
items.statement: A very weakly compatible system R = (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_λ}, {H_τ}) of rank n [ACC+ §7]: M a number field, S a finite set of finite places, monic degree-n Q_v(X) ∈ M[X] for v ∉ S, multisets H_τ for τ : F ↪ M̄, and continuous semisimple r_λ : G_F → GL_n(M̄_λ) with (a) r_λ unramified at v ∉ S, v ∤ l, with char r_λ(Frob_v) = Q_v(X); (b) for l outside a density-0 set, r_λ crystalline with HT_τ = H_τ; (c) HT_τ(det r_λ) = Σ_{h∈H_τ} h. Restriction to F′/F and tensor products over a common M are defined.
items.note: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5 and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5:operations (rank-n systems, restriction and tensor operations). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): S is a set of finite places (p. 51).

items.name: Definition 6.1.2 (1), (2), (4), (5): pure, automorphic, irreducible and strongly irreducible systems
items.statement: R is pure of weight m if |ια|² = q_v^m for the roots of Q_v and H_{cτ} = {m − h : h ∈ H_τ}; automorphic if some regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_n(𝔸_F) and ι : M ↪ ℂ give π_v unramified with rec^T_{F_v}(π_v)(Frob_v) of characteristic polynomial ι(Q_v(X)) for all v ∉ S; irreducible if r_λ is irreducible for l outside a density-0 set; strongly irreducible if R|_{G_{F′}} is irreducible for every finite F′/F.
items.note: PA.5 and R24.5:operations.

items.name: Definition 6.1.2 (3): weakly automorphic of level prime to T
items.statement: For T a finite set of finite places disjoint from S, R is weakly automorphic of level prime to T if there are a regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_n(𝔸_F) and ι : M ↪ ℂ such that for all but finitely many v ∉ S and for every v ∈ T, π_v is unramified and rec^T_{F_v}(π_v)(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial ι(Q_v(X)); weakly automorphic means T = ∅.
items.note: New in this paper (tensor products with poorly controlled ramification). Routed as a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5.

items.name: The compatible system of a regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_2 over a CM field
items.statement: For F CM and π regular algebraic cuspidal of GL_2(𝔸_F) of weight λ there is an associated automorphic very weakly compatible system R = (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_{π,λ}}, {H_τ}) with H_τ = {λ_{τ,1} + 1, λ_{τ,2}} [ACC+ Lem. 7.1.10].
items.note: The HLTT non-self-dual Galois representations are AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.4; the compatible-system packaging is PA.5. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the paper says 'automorphic'.

items.name: Lemma 6.1.3: purity from potential weak automorphy of symmetric powers
items.statement: Let R be a very weakly compatible system of rank 2 with H_τ = {0, m} for all τ, and v_0 ∉ S. If for infinitely many n there is a finite Galois F_n/F with Sym^{n−1}R|_{F_n} weakly automorphic of level prime to {v | v_0}, then the roots α_1, α_2 of Q_{v_0}(X) satisfy |ια|² = q_{v_0}^m for every ι : M̄ ↪ ℂ.
items.note: Proof: the central character of Π is |·|^{n(m−1)(1−n)/2} up to finite order, so Π|·|^{(m−1)(n−1)/2} is unitary; the Jacquet–Shalika bound gives |ια_i| ≤ q_{v_0}^{m/2 + 1/(2(n−1))}; let n → ∞. As in [ACC+ Cor. 7.1.13]. Routed as a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.3). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the embedding is of M̄ (p. 52 image).

items.name: The Jacquet–Shalika bound
items.statement: For a unitary cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) unramified at v, the Satake parameters have absolute value < q_v^{1/2} [JS81 Cor. 2.5].
items.note: Imported analytic input (JS81 is a prerequisite). Routed as a source of ML.3 with the other analytic inputs of the endpoints.

items.name: Lemma 6.1.4: weakly automorphic and pure implies automorphic
items.statement: Let F be CM and R a very weakly compatible system of rank n that is weakly automorphic, via π, and pure of weight m. Then R is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: at v ∈ S′ − S, r_λ ≅ r_ι(π) (Chebotarev) and Varma's local–global compatibility makes π_v a subquotient of the unramified principal series with Satake parameter from Q_v; purity makes it irreducible. Routed as a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5.

items.name: Varma's local–global compatibility away from p
items.statement: [Var24 Thm. 1]: for π regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_n over a CM field and v ∤ p, r_ι(π)|^ss_{W_{F_v}} ≅ ι^{−1}rec^T_{F_v}(π_v)^ss.
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.5 (as for PAPER-QIAN-23).

items.name: Lemma 6.1.5: primes of large image have density one
items.statement: Let R be a strongly irreducible very weakly compatible system of rank 2 over a number field F. The set L(R) of primes l ∉ S such that r_λ is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights H_τ and r̄_λ(G_{F̃}) contains a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_l) for every λ | l (F̃ the Galois closure of F/ℚ) has Dirichlet density 1.
items.note: From [ACC+ Lem. 7.1.3]. Routed as a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5.

items.name: The trichotomy for rank-2 compatible systems
items.statement: [ACC+ Lem. 7.1.2]: an irreducible very weakly compatible system of rank 2 is strongly irreducible, Artin up to twist, or induced from a quadratic extension (from algebraic Hecke characters); distinct Hodge–Tate weights exclude the second case.
items.locator: §7.1, proof of Theorem 7.1.1, p. 61; proof of Theorem 7.2.1, pp. 61–62
items.note: Routed as a source of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the proof of Theorem 7.2.3 (p. 62) also uses it; if [ACC+23, Lemma 7.1.2] assumes R irreducible, Theorem 7.1.1 should state it.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.3: the p–r switch
items.statement: Let F be imaginary CM, m ≥ 2, n ≥ 1, X_0 finite, and R of rank 2 with H_τ = {0, m}, det r_λ = ε^{−m}, strongly irreducible, X_0 ∩ S = ∅, F/ℚ Galois containing an imaginary quadratic F_0. Suppose given: (6) E/ℚ cyclic totally real of degree m, disjoint from F, and Ψ : 𝔸_L^× → M^× (L = EF) with Ψ(α) = Π_i τ_i(N_{L/EF_0}α)^{m−i}cτ_i(N_{L/EF_0}α)^{i−1} and R_CM = Ind Ψ_λ with det = ε^{−m(m−1)/2}; (7) primes p ≠ r away from S with places 𝔭, 𝔯; (8) R_aux of rank m, pure of weight m − 1, with S_aux disjoint from X_0 ∪ {v | pr}, det ε^{−m(m−1)/2}, H = {0, …, m − 1}; (9) S_UA of rank nm, pure of weight nm − 1, det ε^{−nm(nm−1)/2}, H = {0, …, nm − 1}, weakly automorphic of level prime to X_0 ∪ {v | pr}, with S_UA disjoint from X_0 ∪ {v | pr}; and (10)–(17): unramifiedness at X_0 ∪ {v | pr}, p, r > 2nm + 1 with [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1, r split in EF_0 and [L(ζ_r) : L] = r − 1, the residual images (SL_2 ⊂ r̄_𝔭(G_F) ⊂ GL_2 and likewise at 𝔯; r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_F) = GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) with multiplier ε̄^{1−m} if m > 2, GL_2(𝔽_p) if m = 2; r̄_{CM,𝔯}|_{G_{F(ζ_r)}} irreducible; if m = 2 the extensions of F(ζ_p) cut out by the projective representations of r̄_𝔭|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} and r̄_{aux,𝔭}|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} linearly disjoint), s̄_{UA,𝔭} ≅ s̄_{aux,𝔭} and r̄_{aux,𝔯} ≅ r̄_{CM,𝔯}, and the local conditions at v | p (F_v ⊇ ℚ_{p²}, r̄_𝔭|_{G_{F_v}} and ρ̄_{2,m,0}|_{G_{F_v}} trivial; ordinary or ∼ ρ_{2,m,0}, with r̄_{aux,𝔭} trivial, r_aux ∼ ρ_{m,1,0} and s_UA ∼ ρ_{nm,1,0}) and at v | r (trivial residually, r_aux ordinary). Then Sym^{n−1}R is weakly automorphic of level prime to X_0.
items.note: Proof: Theorem 3.2.1 at 𝔭 (Lemmas 5.2.4, 5.1.4) makes S_aux = Sym^{n−1}R ⊗ R_aux weakly automorphic; Theorem 3.2.1 at 𝔯 (Lemmas 5.2.6, 5.1.4, [BLGGT14 p. 530 (5)]) does the same for S_CM = Sym^{n−1}R ⊗ R_CM; cyclic base change [AC89 Ch. 3 Thm. 4.2] and descent as in [ACC+ Prop. 6.5.13] remove R_CM. Routed as a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 (potential automorphy assembly). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): hypotheses the proof uses were restored: S_aux and S_UA disjoint from X_0 ∪ {v | pr}, the m = 2 disjointness in (13), and the residual-triviality conditions in (15) and (16), which Lemma 5.1.4 needs. As printed, (13) for m > 2 contradicts (8b) (sourceIssues E29), and no hypothesis makes r_𝔯 crystalline at v | r, which the proof needs (E30); Theorem 6.2.4 supplies both repairs.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.4: potential weak automorphy of Sym^{n−1}R
items.statement: Let F be imaginary CM and R a very weakly compatible system of rank 2 with H_τ = {0, m} for some m ≥ 2, det r_λ = ε^{−m}, strongly irreducible. For v_0 ∉ S and each n ≥ 1 there is a CM extension F_n/F, Galois over ℚ, with Sym^{n−1}R|_{G_{F_n}} weakly automorphic of level prime to {v | v_0}.
items.note: Proof: construct the data of Proposition 6.2.3 over a tower F_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ F_6 (the construction items below, coalesced with the Dwork Part II) and verify (1)–(17). Routed as a source of ML.2.

items.name: Construction in Theorem 6.2.4: the CM character Ψ and R_CM
items.statement: Choose E/ℚ totally real cyclic of degree m, disjoint from F_1 (the Galois closure of FF_0), with p_0 unramified; an odd prime q_1 splitting completely in L_1 = EF_1 and v_1 | q_1 split as w_1⋯w_m in L_1; by [HSBT10 Lem. 2.2] a Ψ_0 : 𝔸^×_{L_1} → M^× of the infinity type of Proposition 6.2.3(6a), unramified above X_1, with the Ψ_0|_{O^×_{L_{w_i}}} wildly ramified, pairwise distinct and of product 1; then by Lemma 5.3.3 a CM F_2/F_1 and a finite-order twist Ψ_2 of Ψ_0 ∘ N_{L_2/L_1} with det Ind Ψ_{2,λ} = ε^{−m(m−1)/2}; R_CM = {Ind Ψ_{2,λ}}.
items.note: Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII (the switching data).

items.name: Construction in Theorem 6.2.4: the primes N, p, r, q and the fields F_3
items.statement: Choose primes N, p, r and later q ∉ {p, r, p_0} (p, r ∈ L(R|_{G_{F_2}}), prime to v_0v_1) with N > 100nm + 100 unramified in L_2 and M, p ≡ −1 mod N, r ≡ 1 mod N, p, r > 2nm + 1, p split in L_2 and M, r split in L_2(ζ_p) and M, Ψ_2 unramified above p and r; then r̄_𝔭, r̄_𝔯 have images between SL_2 and GL_2, r̄_{CM,𝔯}|_{G_{F_2(ζ_N,ζ_r)}} is absolutely irreducible, and the p-adic places split into Σ^ord and Σ^ss (Berger's theorem). Take a solvable CM F_3/F_2(ζ_N) disjoint from the field B cut out by r̄_𝔭 × r̄_𝔯 × r̄_{CM,𝔯}, adjoin e^{2πi/N} to M, and choose a semistable elliptic curve A/ℚ with good reduction at p, r, p_0 and a prime q > 2nm + 1 split in M with ρ̄_{A,q}(G_{F_3}) = GL_2(𝔽_q) and A good ordinary at q.
items.note: Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): locator corrected (F_3 is introduced on p. 58); q must also avoid p, r and p_0.

items.name: Berger's reduction of two-dimensional crystalline representations of small weight
items.statement: [Ber10 Thm. 3.2.1]: a crystalline r : G_{ℚ_p} → GL_2(ℚ̄_p) with Hodge–Tate weights {0, m}, 1 ≤ m ≤ p − 1, is either ordinary or has r̄|_{G_{ℚ_{p²}}} ≅ ρ̄_{2,m,0} (up to unramified twist).
items.note: Imported (Ber10 is a prerequisite through Theorem 6.2.4). Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII with the switching construction.

items.name: Kisin's local constancy (a Krasner lemma for families)
items.statement: [Kis99 Thm. 5.1]: for t ∈ T_0(O_{F_v}) and c > 0 there is an open ball U_t ∋ t such that for t′ ∈ U_t the representations W_{t,λ} and W_{t′,λ} are isomorphic modulo p^c (the paper's W_{𝔭,t}/(p^c)) (for the finitely many λ considered).
items.note: Imported (Kis99 is a prerequisite). Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the paper reduces modulo p^c; harmless, since c is arbitrary.

items.name: Construction in Theorem 6.2.4: the local data (i)–(v)
items.statement: There is a CM F_4 = K⁺F_3 (K⁺/ℚ totally real Galois with K⁺_v large), disjoint from B′F_3, such that for v | prp_0q the residual representations r̄_𝔭, r̄_𝔯, r̄_{CM,𝔯}, ρ̄_{A,q} are trivial on G_{F_{4,v}} and for k ∈ {m, nm} there are nonempty opens _kΩ_v ⊂ T_0(O_{F_{4,v}}) with: (i) v ∈ Σ^ord: _kW̄_{t,𝔭} trivial, _kW_{t,𝔭} crystalline ordinary, _kW̄_{t,𝔯}, _kW̄_{t,𝔮} trivial; (ii) v ∈ Σ^ss: _kW_{t,𝔭} crystalline with _kW_{t,𝔭} ∼ ρ_{k,1,0}, residuals trivial; (iii) v | r: _kW_{t,𝔯} crystalline ordinary, residuals trivial; (iv) v | p_0: all residuals trivial; (v) v | q: _kW_{t,𝔮} crystalline ordinary, residuals trivial.
items.note: Proof: Propositions 4.2.5–4.2.6 give an ordinary point, Kisin's local constancy with Lemmas 5.1.4–5.1.5 an open ball; for (ii), Lemma 4.4.4 and Lemma 5.1.3 at t = 0. Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII.

items.name: Construction in Theorem 6.2.4: R_aux and S_UA by Moret-Bailly
