items.statement: For m > 2, apply Proposition 4.5.1 to T(r̄_{CM,𝔯}|_{G_{F_4}}) (r ≡ 1 mod N) with f the surjection of π_1^ét(T_{F_4}) onto its image G ⊂ GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) given by W̄_𝔭 (G ⊇ SU_m(𝔽_{p²}), the geometric monodromy of Proposition 4.4.2), F^avoid = B′F_4, S_0 = {p, r, p_0, q} and Ω_v the preimages of _mΩ_v: this gives F_5 and R_aux = {W_{t,λ}} with r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_{F_5}) = G, so r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_{F_5(ζ_p)}) = SU_m(𝔽_{p²}), r̄_{aux,𝔯} ≅ r̄_{CM,𝔯} and the local properties (m = 2 uses a modular curve with level-r structure, left to the reader; item 144). Then apply Proposition 4.5.1 to T(s̄_{aux,𝔭}, Sym^{nm−1}ρ̄_{A,q}|_{G_{F_5}}) (a Hermitian structure being unique over a finite field) to get F_6 and S_UA with s̄_{UA,𝔭} ≅ s̄_{aux,𝔭}, s̄_{UA,𝔮} ≅ Sym^{nm−1}ρ̄_{A,q} and the local properties; F^avoid must then also contain the field cut out by r̄_{aux,𝔭}.
items.note: Coalesced into PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): material correction: the printed f : π_1(T) → GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) and r̄_{aux,𝔭}(G_{F_5}) = GU_m(𝔽_{p²}) are false (they conflict with det r_aux = ε^{−m(m−1)/2}; sourceIssues E29), and the second F^avoid = B′F_5 is too small (E32).

items.name: Automorphy of Sym^{nm−1} of an elliptic curve over F_6
items.statement: For a semistable elliptic curve A/ℚ and F_6 CM Galois over ℚ, Sym^{nm−1}ρ_{A,q}|_{G_{F_6}} is automorphic, associated to a regular algebraic cuspidal representation that is ι-ordinary at q, by [BCDT01], [Die15] (base change to totally real fields), [NT22] (symmetric powers of Hilbert modular forms) and [AC89], or by [CNT23].
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3 (Newton–Thorne symmetric powers; NT22 is PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26) and ML.5 (base change). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): ι-ordinarity at q needs A to have good ordinary reduction at q, which the construction of q arranges.

items.name: Cyclic base change and descent for GL_n
items.statement: [AC89 Ch. 3 Thm. 4.2]: a cuspidal π of GL_{nm}(𝔸_F) with π ≅ π ⊗ (η ∘ det) for η of order m cutting out a cyclic L/F is automorphically induced from a cuspidal Π of GL_n(𝔸_L), with rec_{F_v}(π)|_{W_{L_w}} = ⊕_i rec_{L_w}(Π^{σ^i}).
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5 registers cyclic base change and automorphic induction with exact hypotheses. Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): [AC89] treats cyclic extensions of prime degree; for composite m it is iterated, and cyclic descent is [ACC+23, Prop. 6.5.13].

items.name: The Sato–Tate group ST(π) and Lemma 7.2.2
items.statement: For π non-CM regular algebraic of weight λ with λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,2} = w and ω_π = |·|^{−w}ψ (ψ unitary of type A_0): ST(π) = U_2(ℝ)_a = {g ∈ U_2(ℝ) : det(g)^a = 1} if ψ has finite order a, and U_2(ℝ) otherwise. Lemma 7.2.2: ST(π) is compact, and if π_v is unramified and essentially tempered the GL_2(ℂ)-class of q_v^{−w/2}rec_{F_v}(π_v)(Frob_v) meets ST(π) in a unique ST(π)-class [π_v].
items.note: ML.3 (Sato–Tate groups and equidistribution).

items.name: Serre's equidistribution criterion
items.statement: [Ser98 Ch. I App.]: the classes [π_v] are equidistributed for μ_ST if for every nontrivial irreducible ρ of ST(π) the partial L-function L^{S_π}(π, ρ, s) = Π_{v∉S_π} det(1 − q_v^{−s}ρ([π_v]))^{−1} (absolutely convergent for Re s > 1) continues meromorphically to ℂ, holomorphic and nonvanishing on Re s = 1.
items.note: ML.3 with AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4 (the analytic inputs of the Weyl criterion).

items.name: Breuil submodules and exact sequences of Breuil modules
items.statement: A complex of Breuil modules is exact iff it is exact on the underlying S̄_𝔽-modules and on the M^{p−2} pieces. 𝒩 ⊆ ℳ is a Breuil submodule iff it is a k[u]/u^{ep}-direct summand with N(𝒩) ⊆ 𝒩 and φ(𝒩 ∩ ℳ^{p−2}) ⊆ 𝒩; then 0 → 𝒩 → ℳ → ℳ/𝒩 → 0 is exact [HLM17, Lem. 2.3.2], and conversely.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25.

items.name: The functor T and its restriction to K_∞
items.statement: T(ℳ) := Hom_{k[u]/u^{ep},φ,N}(ℳ, Â)^∨ has dimension equal to the rank of ℳ, and T(ℳ)|G_{K_∞} ≅ T_∞(ℳ) for the underlying Breuil–Kisin module ([HLM17, (A.3.1), Prop. A.3.2]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported; Lemma 2.2.19 depends on it.

items.name: Kisin's Breuil–Kisin modules of crystalline lattices
items.statement: A G_K-stable lattice in a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, h] has a Breuil–Kisin module 𝔐_O of height ≤ h with T(𝔐_O) ≅ ρ|G_{K_∞}, and the functor is fully faithful ([Kis06]; [GLS14, Thm. 3.2(3), Prop. 3.4(3)]; [Kis06, Prop. 1.3.15], [Kis10, Thm. 1.2.1]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. R07.4 constructs Breuil–Kisin modules and separates 'finite-flat, potentially Barsotti–Tate and merely potentially semistable cases'.

items.name: Liu's strongly divisible modules
items.statement: For p > 2 there is an equivalence between lattices in semistable representations with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p − 2] and strongly divisible modules; the reduction of a strongly divisible module is a Breuil module, compatibly with 𝔐_O and with the functor to Galois representations ([Liu08, Thm. 2.3.5, §3.2, §3.4, Cor. 3.3.2]; [EGH13, Prop. 3.1.4, Lem. 3.2.2]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported; no layer of the atlas plans strongly divisible modules.

items.name: Lifting the maximal multiplicative submodule
items.statement: The maximal multiplicative submodule of the dual 𝔐^* of the Breuil–Kisin module of a crystalline lattice lifts that of the reduction ([Kis09, Prop. 1.2.11] with the duality of [Liu07, §3.1]); the paper uses it at height d − 1 as an 'obvious generalization'.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25.

items.name: The extension groups Ext¹_{BrMod^cr} and the restriction maps
items.statement: Ext¹_{BrMod^cr}(ℳ(s; a), ℳ(t; b)) is computed in the exact category of crystalline Breuil modules; with χ₁ := T(ℳ(t; b)), χ₂ := T(ℳ(s; a)), the maps res_K : Ext¹_{BrMod^cr} → Ext¹_{G_K}(χ₂, χ₁) and res_{K∞} : Ext¹_{G_K}(χ₂, χ₁) → Ext¹_{G_{K∞}}(χ₂, χ₁) are 𝔽-linear, the Baer sum corresponding to summing the y_j and μ_j (Remark 2.2.11).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25.

items.name: Peu and très ramifiée classes
items.statement: For K/ℚ_p, H¹(G_K, ε̄) = K^×/K^{×p} by Kummer theory; a class is peu ramifiée if it lies in the image of O_K^×, and très ramifiée otherwise.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. R07.5: 'Prove the extension-class distinctions used in the peu/très ramifiée cases'. Used in the paper without a definition.

items.name: Reductions of crystalline extensions of unramified by cyclotomic are peu ramifiée
items.statement: The reduction of a crystalline representation (ur *; 0 ur·ε^{−1}) is peu ramifiée ([CEGS22b, Lem. A.4]); the same lemma describes the image of (2.2.17) in the peu ramifiée subspace when some r_i ≠ p.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported.

items.name: The corrected Emerton–Gee realisation of extension classes
items.statement: For (t_1, …, t_d) ∈ T(𝔽̄_p), Ext¹_{(t),k} ⊆ Π_i Ext¹_{G_K}(ur_{t_i}ε̄^{i−d}ω_{k,i}, ur_{t_{i+1}}ε̄^{i+1−d}ω_{k,i+1}) is the closed subvariety where every cup product ψ_i ∪ ψ_{i+1} vanishes, and a dense Zariski open U ⊆ Ext¹_{(t),k} consists of classes realised by points of 𝒰^k(𝔽̄_p) (the version of [EG23, Thm. 5.5.12] proved in [EG]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported from the Emerton–Gee errata.

items.name: At a generic point the weight-0 crystalline ring is the ordinary ring
items.statement: For ρ̄ generic, maximally nonsplit and satisfying (2.5.3), R^{crys,0,O}_{ρ̄} equals the ordinary lifting ring of [CHT08, §2.4.2] and is formally smooth over O ([CHT08, Lem. 2.4.7]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. The key claim inside Theorem 2.5.2.

items.name: Ordinary deformation problems and their formal smoothness (CHT08)
items.statement: The ordinary deformation problem of [CHT08, §2.4.2] (upper-triangular lifts with prescribed diagonal characters) is representable and, under the distinctness conditions there, formally smooth ([CHT08, Lem. 2.4.7]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. L7: 'Construct ordinary deformation functors with a full invariant flag and specified graded characters … Prove representability, dimension'.

items.name: Charts and versal rings of algebraic stacks
items.statement: A versal ring at a finite type point of an algebraic stack of finite type is a complete local ring of a smooth chart; complete local rings at finite type points of a generically reduced scheme of finite type over a field are generically reduced ([Sta13, Tags 0DR0, 0CMK, 04YH, 0DR4]; [CEGS22a, Lem. 4.5]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. R09.4 plans algebraic stacks with smooth atlases, R09.6 the relation of deformation functors to completed local rings 'including stabilisers and versality'.

items.name: Components of completed tensor products of local rings
items.statement: If A_1, …, A_r are O-flat complete Noetherian local O-algebras whose irreducible components are geometrically irreducible, the irreducible components of A_1 ⊗̂ ⋯ ⊗̂ A_r and of its special fibre are the products of those of the factors ([BLGHT11, Lem. 3.3]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. As the component lemmas of PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B (item 52): R03.3 'equidimensionality … lemmas', R03.6 'supported on a specified union of components'.

items.name: Kisin's weight-0 crystalline lifting rings
items.statement: R^{crys,0,O}_{ρ̄|G_{F_v}} is O-flat and equidimensional of dimension 1 + n² + (n(n−1)/2)[F_v : ℚ_p], with regular generic fibre ([Kis08, Thms. 3.3.4, 3.3.8]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. L7: 'construct fixed labeled Hodge-type and inertial-type potentially semistable deformation rings … Prove … the Kisin dimension formula'.

items.name: The rings R^1_v and R^χ_v (ACC+)
items.statement: For χ = 1, the generic points of R^1_v/ϖ have unique generalisations; for χ_{v,i} pairwise distinct, R^χ_v is irreducible of dimension 1 + n² with generic point of characteristic 0 ([ACC+23, Props. 6.2.16, 6.2.17]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. L7: 'Give semistable, Steinberg and minimally ramified analogues away from p for rank n'.

items.name: Support propagation for weight-0 patched complexes
items.statement: An automorphic point of Spec R_∞ lies on an irreducible component contained in Spec T_∞; if the generic points of the special fibre of a component C generalise in R′_∞ to the same component as those of such a component, then C ⊂ Spec T_∞; and support on H*(C_∞) descends to support on H*(X_K, O)_𝔪 ([CN23, Prop. 5.4.2, Cor. 5.4.3]; [ACC+23, Cor. 6.3.9]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported from Caraiani–Newton.

items.name: The base-change reduction of Theorem 3.2.1
items.statement: Theorem 3.2.1 follows from Theorem 3.2.5 by a soluble CM base change arranging hypotheses (1)–(8) of §3.2 and soluble descent, 'identical to the one found in [ACC+23, §6.5.12]'.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25.

items.name: Henniart: λ-adic characters with λ-independent traces are algebraic
items.statement: A system of λ-adic characters of a number field with Frobenius traces in a number field M, independent of λ, arises from a Hecke character of type A₀ ([Hen82]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. As the dictionary between type-A₀ Hecke characters and Galois characters (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21, item 128). Review (REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25): the rank-one case (a parallel-weight-m rank-one system is ε^{−m} times a finite-order character) is also used implicitly in Lemma 6.1.3 and Theorem 7.2.1.

items.name: Hodge–Tate weights of the Dwork motives (Qian)
items.statement: HT_τ(V_{t,λ}) = {M_τ, …, M_τ + n − 1} for an integer M_τ ([Qia23, Lem. 3.10]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported from Qian.

items.name: Ordinarity of crystalline representations with parallel weights
items.statement: A crystalline representation of G_{K_v} with parallel Hodge–Tate weights {0, …, n − 1} is ordinary iff the roots of its Frobenius characteristic polynomial have valuations 0, f, …, (n − 1)f ([Ger19, Lem. 2.32]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported.

items.name: Monodromy of the Dwork motives and geometric irreducibility (Qian)
items.statement: If −1 mod N ∉ ⟨l⟩, the geometric monodromy of W̄_λ is SL_n(k(λ)), and Qian's moduli spaces are geometrically irreducible ([Qia23, Lem. 3.7, Prop. 3.8]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported from Qian; the coalesced candidate owns Qian's monodromy layers.

items.name: Uniqueness of nondegenerate Hermitian forms over finite fields
items.statement: For a quadratic extension l/k of finite fields, all nondegenerate Hermitian forms on l^n are equivalent to the identity form ([Lew82, §4]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported.

items.name: The cohomology of the Fermat hypersurface
items.statement: H^{N−2} of the Fermat hypersurface of degree N in ℙ^{N−1} splits under H into lines indexed by characters a = (a_i) with Σa_i = 0 and all a_i ≠ 0, with known Hodge types ([DMOS82, I.7.4]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported.

items.name: Fontaine–Laffaille reduction of crystalline characters
items.statement: A crystalline character of G_{ℚ_{l²}} with Hodge–Tate weights a at τ and b at cτ, 0 ≤ a, b ≤ l − 2, restricts on inertia to ω_τ^a ω_{cτ}^b (with HT(ε) = −1 and geometric Art).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. R07.3 constructs Fontaine–Laffaille theory and 'how torsion subquotients and reductions change the filtration'; R01.2 the fundamental characters.

items.name: The Poincaré-duality pairing on W̄_λ
items.statement: When −1 mod N ∈ ⟨l⟩ there is a perfect sesquilinear pairing ⟨·,·⟩_{W̄_λ} : W̄_λ × W̄_λ → k(λ)(1 − n) with ⟨y, x⟩ = −c⟨x, y⟩, from the alternating cup product on H^{N−2} (N − 2 odd) and the Ψ-twist, extending sesquilinearly to O_{M_λ}-coefficients.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25.

items.name: Jacquet–Shalika: strong multiplicity one and non-vanishing on Re s = 1
items.statement: For cuspidal π, π′ of GL_n(𝔸_F), π ≅ π′ if π_v ≅ π′_v for almost all v, and L^S(π × π′^∨, s) does not vanish on Re s = 1 ([JS81]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.2.3, p. 56; proof of Theorem 7.2.3, p. 62
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. ML.3 'Supply nonvanishing/analytic inputs for the Weyl criterion separately'; item 93 covers only the Jacquet–Shalika bound.

items.name: ACC+ inputs to Theorems 6.2.1 and 7.1.1
items.statement: [ACC+23, Thm. 7.1.1] (the quadratic CM extension trick), [ACC+23, Cor. 7.1.15] (soluble base change of the result), and [ACC+23, Cor. 7.1.12], the case m = 1 of Theorem 6.2.1 (Remark 6.2.2).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 7.1.1, p. 61; Remark 6.2.2, p. 53
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported from PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23, whose endpoints are ML.2/ML.3 sources.

items.name: The analytic step of the Sato–Tate theorem
items.statement: The irreducible representations of the Sato–Tate group are Sym^k ⊗ det^j; potential automorphy of all Sym^k with Brauer induction gives meromorphic continuation and non-vanishing of L^{S_π}(π, ρ, s) on Re s = 1 for every non-trivial irreducible ρ, and Serre's criterion gives equidistribution ([Gee09 §7], [BLGHT11 §8]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. ML.3 plans the 'resulting analytic/equidistribution arguments'; AN.4 'Meromorphic continuation via induction'.

items.name: The Chebotarev density theorem
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension of number fields every conjugacy class is the Frobenius class of a set of primes of positive density.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. As in the other extractions of this series.

items.name: Big-image bookkeeping over F(ζ_p)
items.statement: If SL_2(𝔽_p) ≤ r̄(G_F) ≤ GL_2(𝔽_p), det r̄ = ε̄^{−m} and [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1, then r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) = SL_2(𝔽_p); the unitary analogue gives SU_m(𝔽_{p²}). This feeds hypothesis (13) of Proposition 6.2.3 into Lemmas 5.2.4 and 5.2.6.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Used implicitly.

items.name: Group theory in the big-image lemmas
items.statement: A subdirect product of non-abelian simple groups is a product of some of the factors; Aut(G^k) ≅ Aut(G)^k ⋊ S_k; and Mackey's criterion for the irreducibility of induced representations.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemmas 5.2.4 and 5.2.6, pp. 46–48; proof of Theorem 6.2.4, p. 58
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported (standard).

items.name: Identities for ρ_{n,m,0}
items.statement: Sym^{n−1}ρ_{2,m,0} ≅ ρ_{n,m,0} and ρ_{n,m,0} ⊗ ρ_{m,1,0} ≅ ρ_{nm,1,0} (the summand indexed by k = m(i − 1) + j is ε_2^{nm−k}(ε′_2)^{k−1}).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. The review checked the tensor identity.

items.name: Compatibility of ∼ and ordinarity with the operations
items.statement: The relation ∼ is compatible with Sym^{n−1} and tensor products ([BLGGT14, p. 530, (5)]), and symmetric powers and tensor products of crystalline ordinary representations are crystalline ordinary.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Item 41 lists only restriction, direct sums and tensor products for ∼.

items.name: Algebraic Hecke characters with prescribed local restrictions
items.statement: There is an algebraic Hecke character of L with a given infinity type and prescribed restrictions to O_w^× at finitely many places ([HSBT10, Lem. 2.2]).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Imported.

items.name: The auxiliary system R_aux for m = 2
items.statement: For m = 2 the paper constructs R_aux from a modular curve with level-r structure instead of the Dwork family, as 'a straightforward (and considerably simpler) variant … we leave this case to the reader'.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. Unwritten in the paper; the design job must supply it.

items.name: Symmetric powers of very weakly compatible systems
items.statement: For a very weakly compatible system R of rank 2 with H_τ = {0, m}, Sym^{n−1}R has representations Sym^{n−1}r_λ, weights {0, m, …, (n − 1)m} and determinant det^{n(n−1)/2}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. PA.5 provides 'comparison lemmas for restriction to field extensions, tensor products, duals, characters and symmetric powers'; Definition 6.1.1 defines only restriction and tensor product.

items.name: Irreducibility of unramified principal series
items.statement: An unramified principal series of GL_n(F_v) whose Satake parameters α_i satisfy α_i/α_j ≠ q_v^{±1} is irreducible (Bernstein–Zelevinsky).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25. ET.6 develops 'the needed … segment/Langlands-quotient theory' for GL_m.

prerequisites.citation: P. Allen, F. Calegari, A. Caraiani, T. Gee, D. Helm, B. Le Hung, J. Newton, P. Scholze, R. Taylor and J. A. Thorne, Potential automorphy over CM fields, Ann. of Math. 197 (2023), 897–1113
prerequisites.why: Theorems 2.3.5 and 2.4.10, Definition 4.3.1, §6 (local problems 6.2.15–6.2.17, Lemma 6.2.25, Proposition 6.5.3, Theorem 6.1.1, patching §§6.4–6.5, §6.5.12) and §7 (Lemmas 7.1.2, 7.1.3, 7.1.10, Corollaries 7.1.12–7.1.15, Theorem 7.1.11).

prerequisites.citation: A. Caraiani and J. Newton, On the modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields, preprint, arXiv:2301.10509 (v3, 27 March 2025)
prerequisites.why: Theorems 4.2.15 and 4.3.1 (local–global compatibility at p in weight 0), Lemma 5.3.3, Proposition 5.4.2 and Corollary 5.4.3 in §3.

prerequisites.citation: M. Emerton and T. Gee, Moduli stacks of étale (φ, Γ)-modules and the existence of crystalline lifts, Ann. of Math. Stud. 215 (Princeton, 2023), with the authors' errata (moduli-errata.pdf)
prerequisites.why: Definitions 3.2.1 and 4.8.8, Theorems 4.8.12, 4.8.14, 5.5.12 and 6.5.1, Proposition 4.8.10, §5.5 and Conjecture 8.2.2 in §2.4–2.5.

prerequisites.citation: T. Gee, T. Liu and D. Savitt, The weight part of Serre's conjecture for GL(2), Forum Math. Pi 3 (2015), e2
prerequisites.why: Lemma 5.1.2, Proposition 5.1.3, Lemma 5.4.2, Theorems 5.1.5, 5.4.1, 6.1.18 and Proposition 5.3.4 in §2.2.

prerequisites.citation: M. Emerton, T. Gee and F. Herzig, Weight cycling and Serre-type conjectures for unitary groups, Duke Math. J. 162 (2013), 1649–1722
prerequisites.why: Proposition 3.1.4, Lemma 3.2.2 and Definition 3.2.8 (Breuil modules) in §2.1.

routes.reason: ML.2 assembles potential automorphy, ML.3 owns symmetric powers, Sato–Tate and their analytic consequences, and ML.0 registers infinity types and normalisations. Theorems A–C and 6.2.1, the Sato–Tate group, Serre's criterion, symmetric powers of elliptic curves and cyclic base change are planned there, and this paper is a source for them. Its missing items of the same kind are routed here too: the p–r switch (Proposition 6.2.3, Theorem 6.2.4, as PAPER-QIAN-23 routed its endpoints to ML.2), purity from symmetric powers (Lemma 6.1.3, the Jacquet–Shalika bound), parallel weight with Clozel's purity lemma, and the Bianchi applications E–G with their definitions. Review: accepted. Jacquet–Shalika (strong multiplicity one and non-vanishing), the ACC+ inputs of Theorems 6.2.1 and 7.1.1 were added, with the planned Sato–Tate analytic step and Chebotarev.

R01.4 owns residual-image facts and consumes the finite-group classification results; G7 owns adequacy and the image conditions in rank n. The Taylor–Wiles big-image conditions (Definition 5.2.1), Lemmas 5.2.2–5.2.6 and the adequacy theorem of Guralnick–Herzig–Taylor–Thorne belong inside these layers, where PAPER-QIAN-23 and PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 routed their image lemmas. Review: accepted; the big-image bookkeeping and the group-theoretic inputs of §5.2 were added.

Globalising local characters (Grunwald–Wang) and the Brauer-group obstruction to m-th roots of characters are Hochschild–Serre and Poitou–Tate statements; PAPER-QIAN-23 routed the same obstruction to R02.2 and R02.4. Tau Ceti's class field theory roadmap excludes Grunwald–Wang. Review: accepted.

PA.5 owns very weakly compatible systems and their transport. Weak automorphy of level prime to T (Definition 6.1.2(3)), its upgrade under purity (Lemma 6.1.4), the density of large-image primes (Lemma 6.1.5) and the trichotomy of ACC+ Lemma 7.1.2 are statements about such systems. Review: accepted; symmetric powers of compatible systems (item 145) are planned in PA.5.

R23.1 plans Moret-Bailly's theorem with prescribed local opens, splitting and linear disjointness, which is the first part of Proposition 4.5.1. Its refinement making a given finite quotient of π_1 surjective (Chebotarev for schemes of finite type and Jordan's theorem) belongs in the same layer. Review: accepted.

L7 owns rank-n potentially semistable and Fontaine–Laffaille lifting rings, ordinary conditions and their component maps. The relation 'connects', the local models ρ_{n,m,0} and Lemmas 5.1.3–5.1.5 are component statements about these rings; PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25 routed its 'connects' item to L7 as well. Review: accepted. The ρ_{n,m,0} identities, the compatibility of ∼ and ordinarity with the operations and Geraghty's ordinarity criterion were added. The reviews of PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B and PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 placed BLGGT14's ∼ in PolarizedAutomorphyLifting; L7, the owner of local components, is the better home for a local relation, and this route (like PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25's) keeps it there; the two placements should be reconciled in favour of L7.

routes.title: Local Galois deformation rings and their components, Part II: generic reducedness of weight-zero crystalline lifting rings via Emerton–Gee stacks
routes.brief: Build on Local Galois deformation rings and their components (LocalGaloisDeformationRings), whose L7 constructs Kisin's rank-n potentially semistable lifting rings of fixed labelled Hodge type, their characteristic-zero points and dimension, and whose L8 separates ordinary conditions. This Part II owns §2 of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne, 'The Ramanujan and Sato–Tate conjectures for Bianchi modular forms' (Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025) e10). Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 2.5.5 (Theorem D): if p > d, K/ℚ_p is finite and E/ℚ_p contains the Galois closure of K, then for every ρ̄ : G_K → GL_d(𝔽) the special fibre R^{crys,0,O}_{ρ̄}/ϖ of the weight-0 crystalline lifting ring (Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1, …, d − 1} at every embedding) is generically reduced. Theorem 2.5.2: for p > d the Breuil–Mézard cycle of the special fibre of the Emerton–Gee stack 𝒳_d^{crys,0} is Z^{crys,0} = 𝒳^0_{d,red} (the component of Serre weight 0), so the special fibre is generically reduced. Theorem 2.3.2: a weight-0 crystalline lift of a generic ρ̄ (Definition 2.3.1) is ordinary, upper triangular with diagonal ur_{λ_d}, ur_{λ_{d−1}}ε^{−1}, …, ur_{λ_1}ε^{1−d}. Layers: (1) quasi-Breuil and Breuil modules with 𝔽-coefficients, height ≤ p − 2, monodromy N and the unit c = φ(E(u))/p (use the corrected commutation φ(u^eN(x)) = cN(φ(x)) of sourceIssues E2 and arXiv v3), crystalline Breuil modules, the functor T, Theorem 2.1.4 (exactness, subobject correspondence) and Theorem 2.1.5 (reductions of crystalline lattices of weights in [0, p − 2], through strongly divisible modules); (2) rank-one modules 𝔐(s; a) and M(s; a) (Definitions 2.2.1–2.2.2, Lemma 2.2.3), the extension normal form (Proposition 2.2.4), the crystallinity constraint (Lemma 2.2.7), the invariants n_i, r_i (Lemma 2.2.13), restriction to K_∞ (Lemma 2.2.15), Lemmas 2.2.18–2.2.19 and generic classes (Definition 2.2.26); (3) generic ρ̄, Theorem 2.3.2 and Corollary 2.3.3 (peu ramifiée extensions); (4) the Emerton–Gee stack 𝒳_d, its weight-0 crystalline substack and versal rings (Proposition 2.4.1), Serre weights, maximally nonsplit representations of niveau one (with the index correction of sourceIssues E4 and the ur_ν convention of E3) and the classification of components with generic points (Theorem 2.4.3, using the Emerton–Gee errata); (5) the cycle Z^{crys,0} and Theorem 2.5.2 (sourceIssues E5); (6) the passage from the stack to lifting rings (smooth charts, flat base change of scheme-theoretic images, CEGS Lemma 4.5) and Theorem 2.5.5; record the sharpness remarks 2.5.6–2.5.7 as non-claims. The Emerton–Gee stacks are imported from Emerton–Gee's monograph (a prerequisite); do not re-plan them here. Imports: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory (R07.3 Fontaine–Laffaille, R07.4 Breuil–Kisin modules, R07.5 residual types); PadicHodgeTheory (R06.2 Hodge–Tate weights, P7 étale (φ, Γ)-modules); LocalGaloisDeformationRings (L7, L8, R08.1, R08.3); Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.4, R09.6: algebraic stacks and versal deformations); Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1). Consumer: WeightZeroCrystallineAutomorphyLifting (Lemma 3.2.4(2)).

routes.title: Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields, Part II: weight-zero crystalline automorphy lifting with p arbitrarily ramified
routes.brief: Build on Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure), whose PA.3 compares patched complexes and proves the generic support implication of derived Ihara avoidance, and whose PA.4 constructs Taylor–Wiles data and ultrapatching. This Part II owns §3 of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne (Forum Math. Pi 13 (2025) e10). Final theorem, as the paper states it. Theorem 3.2.1: let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field, p > n prime, and ρ : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) continuous with (1) ρ unramified almost everywhere; (2) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} crystalline of weight 0 (HT_τ = {0, …, n − 1}) for every v | p; (3) ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, with ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} of adequate image; (4) some σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar; (5) a cuspidal π of GL_n(𝔸_F), regular algebraic of weight 0, with ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π) and, for v | p, π_v unramified and r_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ ρ|_{G_{F_v}}. Then ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for a cuspidal Π of weight 0, unramified at every v | p and wherever ρ and π are both unramified. Layers: (1) Caraiani–Newton's local–global compatibility at p in weight 0 with arbitrary ramification (their Theorems 4.2.15 and 4.3.1), imported from arXiv 2301.10509 as a prerequisite; (2) the setting of §3.2 (hypotheses (1)–(8), level K, problems S_χ with D^{crys,0}_v at S_p and D^χ_v at R) and Proposition 3.2.3 (Hecke-valued Galois representations with a nilpotent ideal of exponent δ(n, [F:ℚ])); (3) Lemma 3.2.4 on the completed tensor products of local rings, where part (2) takes Theorem D from the sibling Part II WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings together with Caraiani–Newton Lemma 5.3.3 (generically reduced special fibre gives unique generalisation of generic points); (4) the weight-0 patched objects and Theorem 3.2.5 (support is preserved when ρ_1|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ ρ_2|_{G_{F_v}} for v | p), with Caraiani–Newton Proposition 5.4.2 and Corollary 5.4.3; (5) the base change argument of ACC+ §6.5.12 giving Theorem 3.2.1; (6) the adequate-image ordinary theorem of Miagkov–Thorne (Theorem 1.3), used in §6. Imports: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.3, PA.4; Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8, P9); Global Galois deformation rings (GlobalGaloisDeformations G8); LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 (D^χ_v, 'connects'); Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.0–ALS.4); Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2, IHG.3, IHG.5); Reusable infrastructure for torsion in arithmetic cohomology (TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.4); AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.5; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.4, AG2.7; ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7. Coordinate with the pending AutomorphyLiftingBeyondTaylorWiles (conditional lifting over arbitrary number fields) and PolarizedAutomorphyLifting.
routes.reason: The atlas plans generic patching and support (PA.3, PA.4, P8, P9) and local–global compatibility at p only in the Fontaine–Laffaille and ordinary cases (PA.1, PA.2). It has no layer for Caraiani–Newton's weight-0 crystalline compatibility with arbitrary ramification, nor for the lifting theorem built on it. The two pending Part IIs of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure are conditional lifting over arbitrary number fields (AutomorphyLiftingBeyondTaylorWiles) and polarized lifting (PolarizedAutomorphyLifting); neither is this unconditional, unpolarized CM-field theorem. The review may merge the three lifting Part IIs into one. Review: accepted as a separate Part II. PolarizedAutomorphyLifting is polarized (definite unitary groups), and AutomorphyLiftingBeyondTaylorWiles is conditional lifting over arbitrary number fields; Theorem 3.2.1 is unconditional, unpolarized and needs the Caraiani–Newton weight-0 compatibility, so merging would mix three different settings. Caraiani–Newton's support propagation and the base-change reduction of ACC+ §6.5.12 were added.

Pi 13 (2025) e10) use Qian's non-self-dual Dwork motives (N > 100n + 100, N odd, (N, n) = 1, the character χ of [Qia23 Lem. 3.1]) and add the following, to be planned as further layers of the same package. (e) The switching data of Theorem 6.2.4: R_CM from a CM Hecke character (via Lemma 5.3.3), the primes N, p ≡ −1, r ≡ 1, q, the local data (i)–(v) (Kisin's local constancy, Berger's reduction theorem, Lemmas 5.1.3–5.1.5), and R_aux, S_UA from Moret-Bailly (Proposition 4.5.1 in PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1).
